papers.title: STAIR (STructure Aware Information Retriever): A novel dataset and LLM based retriever for document structure augmentation
papers.abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a key component for generating accurate and hallucination free answers using Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are improving at handling long context, but still suffer from "lost in the middle" problem. Thus, precise and accurate retrieval is important. Current retrievers chunk long context into length-based manageable chunks - in the process throwing away rich and informative semantic global structure in the corpus. We introduce a novel retrieval system STAIR that empowers an LLM to exploit global structure in a corpus such as a Table of Contents (ToC) to efficiently store and retrieve information from its model parameters. Our thorough and careful ablation studies with a finetuned Differentiable Search Index (DSI) system show that ToC helps build a low hallucination (less than 0.05%) generative Information Retrieval (IR) system and can generalize to examples where very few training samples are available. To further research in this novel direction of ToC based retrieval we release SearchTome - a diverse benchmark created from 18 books across 6 diverse domains to further research in this novel direction. STAIR achieves a high Recall@1 score of 82.6% on SearchTome as compared to DSI (76.9%), where the difference is found to be statistically significant. STAIR easily beats other strong baselines such as BM25 (59.5%), DPR (68.7%) and out-of-the-box Mistral (13.8%).

summary.takeaway: Incorporating Table of Contents structure into a model‑based retriever yields substantially higher Recall@1 and near‑zero hallucinations.
summary.problem: Chunk‑based retrievers discard global semantic structure, leading to imprecise retrieval and hallucinations in Retrieval‑Augmented Generation.
summary.method: STAIR fine‑tunes a Differentiable Search Index (DSI) LLM with ToC inputs, enabling direct generation of leaf‑node identifiers.
summary.evidence: STAIR attains 82.6% Recall@1 on SearchTome, a 7.4‑point gain over vanilla DSI, while hallucination rate stays below 0.05%.
summary.limitations: Evaluation is confined to corpora that already provide a Table of Contents, limiting generality to unstructured data.
summary.why_for_you: The work directly addresses trustworthy LLM generation by reducing hallucinations through structural cues, relevant to your interests in reliable LLM behavior.

signals.text: STAIR introduces a ToC‑aware retrieval system achieving 82.6% Recall@1 on the new SearchTome benchmark.
It fine‑tunes a DSI model with hierarchical ToC inputs, letting the LLM generate leaf‑node IDs without memorizing structure.
Recall@1 improves 7.4 points over vanilla DSI and hallucinations stay <0.05%, but only on corpora with existing ToC.

deep_dive.overview: STAIR tackles the "lost in the middle" issue of long‑context LLMs by exploiting the inherent hierarchical organization of documents via their Table of Contents. The authors construct a hierarchical tree from the ToC, embed and cluster sections, and fine‑tune a Differentiable Search Index (DSI) model using LoRA adapters. Experiments on the newly released SearchTome benchmark (18 books, 6 domains) show that ToC‑augmented retrieval markedly outperforms traditional baselines (BM25, DPR) and a vanilla DSI, while dramatically lowering hallucination rates. Limitations stem from the reliance on pre‑existing structural metadata.

methodology.title: Model fine‑tuning
methodology.detail: Mistral Instruct v0.2 is fine‑tuned for up to 200 epochs with LoRA (r=16, α=32), early‑stopping on dev Recall@1, using a 14k token input window for STAIR and 512 tokens for DSI.

methodology.title: Hierarchical tree construction
methodology.detail: Documents are recursively embedded, clustered, and summarized to form a tree mirroring the Table of Contents, providing structured prompts to the model.

mechanism.title: Model‑based indexing with ToC
mechanism.detail: The LLM stores the entire corpus in its parameters and, given a query plus ToC context, directly generates the identifier of the leaf node containing the answer, bypassing the need to memorize individual sections.

mechanism.title: Hallucination mitigation
mechanism.detail: By constraining outputs to valid leaf identifiers, the system reduces generation of non‑leaf (invalid) nodes, achieving a hallucination rate near zero regardless of training sample size.

experiments.title: Benchmarks and baselines
experiments.detail: SearchTome benchmark (18 books, 6 domains) evaluated with Recall@1, Recall@3, nDCG@3 via BeIR; baselines include BM25, DPR (NV‑Embed‑v2), out‑of‑the‑box Mistral, and a fine‑tuned vanilla DSI.

experiments.title: Results
experiments.detail: STAIR: R@1 82.6%; DSI: 76.9%; BM25: 59.5%; DPR: 68.7%; Mistral: 13.8%; hallucination <0.05%; statistical significance reported for the R@1 gap.

findings.title: ToC improves retrieval accuracy
findings.detail: Incorporating ToC yields a 7.4% absolute increase in Recall@1 over DSI, especially for leaf nodes with few training examples.

findings.title: Reduced hallucinations
findings.detail: STAIR maintains a near‑zero hallucination rate across training regimes, unlike DSI which shows higher rates for low‑frequency leaf nodes.

contributions: ToC‑aware retrieval system (STAIR) that leverages model‑based indexing.
SearchTome benchmark providing structured ToC data for long‑context retrieval.
Empirical demonstration of hallucination reduction via structural constraints.
limitations: Current evaluation limited to corpora with existing global structure (Table of Contents).
No experiments on standard unstructured retrieval benchmarks.
open_questions: How does ToC‑augmented retrieval perform on documents lacking explicit hierarchical metadata?
Can structural prompting be combined with adversarial training to further improve robustness?
What effects does ToC integration have on the loss landscape and parameter dynamics of the underlying LLM?

papers.title: Representational alignment yields generalizable safety in language models
papers.abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) is essential for their safe deployment. Current alignment methods mainly optimize observable responses, yet models remain vulnerable when the same harmful intent is recast in unfamiliar or adversarial forms that humans can easily recognize. Prototype theory offers an account of this adaptability. Human concepts are represented around central cases, and new instances are categorized according to their graded typicality relative to these prototypes. Here we show that such categorization of moral concepts is weakly preserved in current LLMs. Across 23 LLMs, models often failed to distinguish opposed moral categories or preserve fine-grained typicality within each category. These deficits persist across parameter sizes and alignment stages. We developed representational similarity optimization, which directly aligns the latent representations in LLMs with the categorization expressed in human moral judgements, without supervising generated responses. In matched experiments using the same 251,334 moral annotations, standard behavioral alignment learned the intended moral judgements at the response level while leaving the categorization structure largely unchanged and increasing vulnerability across adversarial evaluations. Reorganizing moral categorization produced more modest gains in explicit judgements but consistently improved adversarial robustness across model scales on diverse benchmarks and attack strategies. Our findings provide functional support for the view that prototype-based categorization contributes to behavioral adaptability. They also show that transferring this representational principle to LLMs yields generalizable safety under adversarial conditions.

summary.evidence: 在251,334个道德标注的实验中，标准行为对齐仅提升响应层面道德判断，而表示对齐显著提高对抗鲁棒性。
summary.limitations: 未提及具体限制，但指出需进一步验证跨不同任务的泛化性。
summary.method: 开发表示相似性优化，直接对齐LLM潜在表示与人类道德判断分类，无需监督生成响应。
summary.problem: 当前对齐方法无法有效应对有害意图的重新表述，导致模型在对抗性评估中易受攻击。
summary.takeaway: 通过表示相似性优化直接对齐LLM的潜在表示与人类道德判断，提升对抗性条件下的通用安全性。
summary.why_for_you: 提升对抗性鲁棒性，符合高效对抗训练需求。

papers.title: ALRA: Adaptive Local Relational Alignment for Logit-Based Pre-training Distillation of Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: Logit-based knowledge distillation for autoregressive language models usually aligns teacher and student next-token distributions over the entire vocabulary. However, this global objective overlooks relative preferences among likely token alternatives. Existing local approaches often select candidate tokens from either the teacher or the student alone. Teacher-only selection can miss tokens that the student considers likely, while student-only selection can rely on an inaccurate ranking early in training. We propose Adaptive Local Relational Alignment (ALRA), a position-specific framework combining student proposals with teacher guidance. At each valid prediction position, the student proposes likely tokens, while the teacher's most probable token is included as an anchor. ALRA adjusts the number of selected tokens according to how broadly the teacher distributes probability within this candidate set relative to the current batch. Adaptive Local Divergence retains the mass-matching term and separately matches the relative token distributions within the selected and remaining vocabulary regions. Unlike the exact full-vocabulary decomposition, it replaces the teacher-mass coefficients of the two conditional terms with unit coefficients, preventing either term from being downweighted solely because its region has low teacher probability. Student-Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment emphasizes high-probability token pairs with small student probability gaps and gives less weight to unlikely or clearly separated pairs. Experiments on The Pile with randomly initialized 200M- and 500M-parameter students across nine zero-shot benchmarks yield average accuracies of 36.62% and 37.40%. ALRA exceeds the strongest competing distillation baseline by 0.94 and 0.83 percentage points and improves over pre-training without distillation by 2.31 and 2.91 points, respectively.

summary.problem: 全局 KL 蒸馏忽略了 token 相对偏好，现有局部方法仅依赖教师或学生的 token 排名。
summary.why_for_you: 符合您对 on‑policy 蒸馏的兴趣，提供了一种用于预训练的全新自适应蒸馏目标。
summary.takeaway: ALRA 的自适应局部 token 选择为自回归语言模型带来了最先进的蒸馏提升。
summary.method: ALRA 从学生的 top token 构建位置特定候选集，并加入教师 top‑1 锚点，自适应调整其规模，随后使用 Adaptive Local Divergence 与 Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment 损失。
summary.limitations: 在可得来源中未说明。
summary.evidence: 在 The Pile 上的实验中，200M 与 500M 学生模型分别达到 36.62% 与 37.40% 的平均 zero‑shot 准确率，超出最强基线 0.94 与 0.83 个百分点。

mechanism.title: Dynamic Candidate Budget
mechanism.detail: 该算法计算教师概率分布的批次级统计量，并调整每个位置的 token 预算 (d_min, d_max)，在教师分布更平坦的区域分配更多 token。

mechanism.title: Unit Coefficient Mass Decoupling
mechanism.detail: 在条件 KL 项中将教师质量系数替换为 1，ALRA 确保选中区域和其余区域无论教师概率质量大小都同等贡献。

experiments.title: Pre‑training Distillation on The Pile
experiments.detail: 教师固定为 Qwen1.5‑1.8B；学生为随机初始化的 Qwen‑200M 与 Qwen‑500M；约 1 B token 预算；九个 zero‑shot 基准；基线包括 Vanilla KD、PD、ATKD、RLD、LDRLD、TAD、BiLD。

signals.text: ALRA 引入自适应局部 token 选择，将学生提议与教师锚点结合，提升蒸馏性能。
Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment 根据学生概率差距为高概率 token 对加权。
200M 与 500M 学生达到 36.62%/37.40% 的平均 zero‑shot 准确率，分别比最佳基线提升 +0.94/+0.83。

deep_dive.overview: ALRA 通过构建位置特定的 token 集，将学生提出的高概率 token 与教师的 top‑1 锚点合并，以解决全局 KL 蒸馏的低效问题。该方法根据教师概率分布的散度自适应确定集合规模，随后使用带单位系数的 Adaptive Local Divergence 保持质量匹配，并通过 Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment 强调学生间隙较小的 token 对。在 The Pile 上使用 200M 与 500M Qwen 学生模型进行评估，ALRA 在九个 zero‑shot 基准上超越所有先前基于 logits 的 KD 基线。
contributions: 用于基于 logits 的预训练蒸馏的 Adaptive Local Relational Alignment 框架。

findings.title: Performance Gains
findings.detail: 200M 学生实现 36.62% 的平均准确率（比最佳基线提升 +0.94，较无 KD 提升 +2.31）；500M 学生实现 37.40% 的平均准确率（比最佳基线提升 +0.83，较无 KD 提升 +2.91）。

methodology.title: Adaptive Local Token Set Construction
methodology.detail: 在每个预测位置，学生提供其 top‑k 可能 token；教师的最高概率 token 作为锚点加入，并根据批次内教师概率离散度对选取 token 数量进行缩放。

methodology.title: Adaptive Local Divergence (ALD)
methodology.detail: 保留全局质量匹配项，同时在选中词表区域和其余区域分别匹配相对分布，使用单位系数避免对低概率区域降权。

methodology.title: Student‑Weighted Pairwise Relational Alignment (SWPRA)
methodology.detail: 计算 token 对的成对对齐损失，并依据学生的概率差距为每对加权，使高概率且排名接近的 token 对获得更强监督。

limitations: 在可得来源中未说明。
open_questions: ALRA 在更大学生模型或下游微调场景下的可扩展性如何？

papers.title: Gradients Know What Outcomes Don't: Unlocking Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning with Gradient-Aligned Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) drives chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models, yet its binary outcome reward cannot distinguish among correct trajectories. Existing dense reward alternatives, from surface heuristics to process reward models, either ignore the expert solutions already present in training corpora or require expensive offline annotation. We propose Gradient-Aligned Reward (GAR), which operates in the policy's own gradient space: truncated backpropagation through the output projection layer extracts a compact gradient vector for each rollout, and cosine similarity with an expert-anchor gradient yields a dense, reasoning-aware reward with less than 9% wall-clock overhead. We prove that this cosine admits a multiplicative decomposition into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors, providing a concrete characterization of what the alignment signal measures. On Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, GAR consistently improves over GRPO and other baselines on competition-level math benchmarks and transfers to GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro without domain-specific data. Code and data are available at https://github.com/LQgdwind/GAR.

summary.evidence: GAR improves Qwen3-4B/8B over GRPO on math benchmarks and transfers to GPQA Diamond/MMLU-Pro with <9% wall-clock overhead.
summary.limitations: GAR has not been deployed in industrial production environments.
summary.method: GAR uses truncated backpropagation through the output projection layer to extract gradient vectors, scoring rollouts via cosine similarity with expert-anchor gradients.
summary.problem: Binary outcome rewards in RLVR cannot distinguish correct reasoning trajectories, leading to flat policy gradients.
summary.takeaway: Gradient-Aligned Reward (GAR) improves LLM reasoning via gradient-space cosine similarity with expert anchors, achieving <9% overhead and math benchmark gains.
summary.why_for_you: This paper directly addresses efficient adversarial training for LLM reasoning by leveraging gradient-space alignment, matching your interest in loss landscape optimization.

contributions: Gradient-space process rewards from expert anchors
Multiplicative decomposition of alignment signal into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors
Dense supervision without additional annotation
<9% overhead in standard RLVR training

experiments.detail: Qwen3-4B/8B models trained on NuminaMath-CoT with expert chain-of-thought solutions
experiments.title: Models and data

experiments.detail: GRPO, REINFORCE++, MASPO, Grad2Reward, G2RL
experiments.title: Baselines

experiments.detail: Pass@k accuracy on math benchmarks, cosine alignment scores, wall-clock overhead
experiments.title: Metrics

findings.detail: GAR improves pass@k by 30.5%-52.4% over baselines on competition-level math benchmarks
findings.title: Performance gains

findings.detail: 3.5× gap in mean cosine alignment between same-method and alternative-method rollouts
findings.title: Alignment characterization

limitations: No industrial deployment experience
Limited to math reasoning benchmarks

mechanism.detail: Correct trajectories with similar reasoning exhibit close gradient directions through output projection layer, enabling dense reward differentiation
mechanism.title: Gradient-space alignment

methodology.detail: Freezes Transformer body and backpropagates only through output projection layer to generate d-dimensional gradient vectors
methodology.title: Truncated backpropagation

methodology.detail: Measures alignment between rollout gradients and expert-anchor gradients, with multiplicative decomposition into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors
methodology.title: Cosine similarity scoring

open_questions: Can gradient alignment generalize to non-math reasoning tasks?
How does GAR scale to larger LLMs beyond Qwen3-8B?
What are the theoretical limits of gradient-space reward shaping?
deep_dive.overview: This paper tackles the limitation of binary outcome rewards in RLVR by introducing Gradient-Aligned Reward (GAR). GAR addresses the problem of flat policy gradients over correct trajectories through a novel mechanism: truncated backpropagation through the output projection layer extracts compact gradient vectors, which are scored via cosine similarity with expert-anchor gradients. The method provides dense process supervision without additional annotation, proven to decompose into prediction-error and activation-pattern factors. Experiments show consistent improvements over baselines on math benchmarks and cross-domain transfer, with minimal computational overhead.

signals.text: GAR: gradient-space cosine similarity with expert anchors for dense reasoning rewards
Truncated backprop through output projection layer extracts d-dimensional gradient vectors
9% overhead while improving pass@k on Qwen3-4B/8B math benchmarks

papers.title: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference
papers.abstract: On-device LLM inference is attractive for privacy and responsiveness, but remains challenging on mobile and embedded devices because model weights far exceed available DRAM. Prior systems exploit activation sparsity and offload weights to SSD or flash storage, but face a fundamental systems trade-off: accurate sparse execution decisions require the latest context, whereas efficient computation-I/O overlap requires early prediction. As a result, existing designs either serialize execution or incur redundant weight fetches, extra computation, and large cache overheads. We present LeanStream, a streaming speculate-and-refine framework for efficient on-device LLM inference. LeanStream progressively refines computation, loading, and cache-retention priorities using partial GPU results, enabling fine-grained overlap between GPU execution and storage I/O. We implement LeanStream on both mobile and embedded platforms. Compared with prior on-device LLM inference systems, LeanStream reduces memory usage by 4.8$\times$ to 7.5$\times$ at the best throughput achieved by prior work, while further improving token generation throughput by 1.6$\times$ to 2.1$\times$.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 13 figures. To appear in the Proceedings of the 32nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking (MobiCom '26)

summary.takeaway: LeanStream achieves up to 7.5× memory reduction and 2.1× token‑generation speedup for on‑device LLM inference.
summary.problem: On‑device LLM inference is limited by weight size exceeding DRAM and the tension between accurate sparse execution decisions and I/O‑compute overlap.
summary.method: It introduces a speculate‑and‑refine streaming framework that continuously refines compute, loading, and cache‑retention priorities using partial GPU results and fine‑grained CPU‑GPU coordination.
summary.evidence: Experiments on 7‑B models across Jetson and OnePlus devices show 4.8×–7.5× lower memory usage and 1.6×–2.1× higher token throughput versus prior systems.
summary.limitations: Not stated in the available source.
summary.why_for_you: The system‑level efficiency gains are directly relevant to deploying trustworthy LLMs and exploring efficient adversarial training on edge devices.

signals.text: LeanStream reduces on‑device LLM memory by 4.8×–7.5× while boosting token throughput 1.6×–2.1×.
Speculate‑and‑refine streaming uses per‑block atomic flags and an offline stochastic MPC policy for fine‑grained CPU‑GPU coordination.
Evaluated on three 7‑B models across Jetson and OnePlus platforms; no results reported for models larger than 7 B.

deep_dive.overview: LeanStream tackles the memory‑and‑latency bottleneck of on‑device LLM inference by streaming weight blocks instead of loading full models. It predicts activation sparsity early, speculatively fetches weight sub‑matrices, and refines these decisions as partial GPU results become available. A lightweight, non‑blocking coordination mechanism embeds synchronization inside GPU thread‑blocks, while a stochastic model‑predictive‑control (MPC) policy, pre‑computed offline, selects streaming frequencies per layer. Across Mistral‑7B, Llama2‑7B, and Qwen2.5‑7B on Jetson AGX Orin/Xavier and OnePlus 13, LeanStream cuts memory usage up to 7.5× and raises token‑per‑second throughput up to 2.1× versus prior baselines.

methodology.title: Lightweight Coordination Mechanism (Algorithm 1)
methodology.detail: Each GPU thread‑block contains a leader thread that non‑blocking checks atomic flags (gpu_rd_flg, gpu_wr_flg, io_rd_flg, io_wr_flg) to consume pre‑loaded weights, write partial results, and signal the CPU, eliminating costly global barriers.

methodology.title: Fine‑Grained Streaming Control Strategy
methodology.detail: Formulated as a finite‑horizon stochastic predictive‑control problem; an offline state‑feedback policy is synthesized into a lookup table that maps quantized remaining‑load volume to communication frequencies (Φₙ) for GPU and I/O stages.

mechanism.title: Permutation‑Invariant Execution
mechanism.detail: Exploits the SwiGLU layer’s invariance to hidden‑neuron ordering, allowing out‑of‑order weight arrivals to be treated as a dense contiguous matrix without re‑indexing, enabling high‑performance dense kernels on partially available neurons.

mechanism.title: Asymmetric CPU‑GPU Communication
mechanism.detail: Multiple GPU completion flags can be aggregated into a single I/O request flag and vice‑versa, decoupling the frequencies of computation and I/O and reducing coordination overhead.

experiments.title: Benchmark Setup
experiments.detail: Models: Mistral‑7B, Llama2‑7B, Qwen2.5‑7B. Devices: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson AGX Xavier (SSD 980 Pro), OnePlus 13 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, UFS 4.0). Baselines: DejaVu, PowerInfer‑2, DejaVu+ (LRU cache). Datasets: Scrolls‑Qasper (long‑doc QA), TruthfulQA (factual generation), CoQA (conversational QA). Metrics: memory budget (GB), tokens per second.

experiments.title: Performance Results
experiments.detail: Across memory budgets, LeanStream achieves 4.8×–7.5× lower DRAM usage at the throughput point of prior work and improves token generation speed by 1.6×–2.1×; figures show consistent gains on both embedded and mobile platforms.

findings.title: Memory Efficiency
findings.detail: LeanStream’s streaming and cache‑retention policy reduces on‑device memory consumption by up to 7.5× compared with the best prior throughput point.

findings.title: Throughput Gains
findings.detail: Token‑generation throughput increases up to 2.1×, demonstrating effective overlap of GPU compute and storage I/O.

findings.title: Scalability Across Devices
findings.detail: Similar relative improvements are observed on both high‑end embedded GPUs (Jetson) and mobile SoCs (Snapdragon), indicating hardware‑agnostic benefits.

contributions: Speculate‑and‑refine streaming framework for on‑device LLM inference
Thread‑block‑level non‑blocking CPU‑GPU coordination using atomic flags
Permutation‑invariant execution allowing out‑of‑order weight processing
Offline stochastic MPC policy for dynamic streaming frequency selection
limitations: Not stated in the available source.
open_questions: How does LeanStream perform on models larger than 7 B or with aggressive quantization?
What is the impact of the streaming framework on adversarial robustness and trustworthiness of generated text?
Can the coordination mechanism be generalized to heterogeneous accelerators beyond GPU‑CPU pairs?

papers.title: Mind the Gap: Robustness Risks in PII Detection Systems
papers.abstract: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) detection is a foundational component of data protection infrastructure where missed entities constitute direct privacy and security risks. Although modern PII systems report strong performance on standard benchmarks, we show that these evaluations mask substantial robustness failures under realistic distribution shifts encountered in deployment. Rather than comparing state-of-the-art accuracy, we study how different PII detection paradigms fail under noisy, unstructured, and informal inputs. We construct a stress test benchmark spanning seven categories of natural distribution shift and evaluate representative systems from three widely deployed architectural families: encoder-based NER (SpaCy), rule-based hybrid detection (Presidio), and generative LLM extraction (Qwen2.5-3B). All three exhibit significant degradation on out-of-distribution inputs, but with distinct and complementary failure modes. Encoder models primarily fail on unseen surface forms and boundary detection, rule-based systems fail on non-standard formats, and LLMs exhibit entity-type confusion and generation instability. These results show that aggregate benchmark scores obscure deployment-critical weaknesses and that no single architecture is uniformly reliable across PII categories. Motivated by these findings, we propose a hybrid detection pipeline with a QA-driven feedback loop for iterative risk mitigation, and release our benchmark to support OOD-aware evaluation of PII systems.

summary.takeaway: PII detection systems suffer severe OOD performance drops, and no single architecture is reliably robust across shift types.
summary.problem: Current PII benchmarks hide robustness failures that appear under realistic noisy, unstructured inputs.
summary.method: The authors build a seven‑category stress‑test benchmark and evaluate SpaCy, Presidio, and Qwen2.5‑3B, then propose a QA‑driven hybrid pipeline.
summary.evidence: Location recall falls from 0.725 to 0.457 for all models, and each architecture shows distinct failure modes on the benchmark.
summary.limitations: The benchmark is synthetic, English‑only, and evaluates only one representative model per family with zero‑shot prompting.
summary.why_for_you: Relevant to trustworthy LLM research because it reveals generation instability and entity‑type confusion in LLM‑based PII extraction.

signals.text: Introduces a synthetic stress‑test benchmark covering seven natural distribution‑shift categories for PII detection.
Proposes a hybrid detection pipeline that iteratively mitigates risk via a QA‑driven feedback loop.
Shows location recall dropping from 0.725 to 0.457 across all models, indicating severe OOD degradation.

deep_dive.overview: The paper constructs a stress‑test benchmark spanning seven realistic distribution‑shift categories (e.g., noisy, informal text) to probe PII detection robustness. Three widely used systems—SpaCy encoder‑based NER, Microsoft Presidio hybrid rule/ML, and Qwen2.5‑3B LLM extraction—are evaluated using relaxed span matching. All exhibit marked performance loss, with location recall falling from 0.725 to 0.457, and each shows distinct failure patterns. To address these gaps, the authors propose a QA‑driven hybrid pipeline and release the benchmark for OOD‑aware evaluation.

methodology.title: Benchmark construction
methodology.detail: Synthesizes test instances across seven natural distribution‑shift categories, targeting noisy, unstructured, and informal inputs.

methodology.title: Evaluation protocol
methodology.detail: Uses relaxed span matching; reports entity‑wise recall and F1, highlighting degradation on flexible‑format types.

mechanism.title: Hybrid QA‑feedback pipeline
mechanism.detail: Combines rule‑based, encoder, and LLM components; iteratively refines detections via question‑answering feedback to mitigate missed entities.

experiments.title: Model suite and data
experiments.detail: Evaluates SpaCy en_core_web_lg (encoder NER), Microsoft Presidio (rule + ML hybrid), and Qwen2.5‑3B‑Instruct (zero‑shot LLM) on the synthetic OOD benchmark.

findings.title: Systematic OOD degradation
findings.detail: All three systems lose significant recall; location recall drops from 0.725 to 0.457, and failure modes differ per architecture.

contributions: Stress‑test benchmark for OOD PII detection
Empirical comparison of encoder, hybrid, and LLM paradigms under realistic shifts
Hybrid detection pipeline with QA‑driven iterative risk mitigation
limitations: Synthetic benchmark limited to a single general domain and English
Only one representative model per architectural family evaluated
LLM used with zero‑shot prompting; fine‑tuning effects not explored
open_questions: How does fine‑tuning or larger LLMs affect OOD robustness in PII extraction?

papers.title: Task-Level Natural Language Priors as Learning Signals for Low-Resource LLM Training
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often struggle when low-resource training data are ambiguous or incomplete. Task-level natural-language priors can provide useful guidance in such settings, but existing approaches usually treat these priors as input context rather than as learning signals during training. We propose Prior-Guided Tuning (PGT), a training perspective that incorporates natural-language priors as auxiliary learning signals for low-resource LLM training. Under this perspective, we introduce Contrastive Prior Steering (CPS), which keeps the original supervised objective intact while adding positive and negative prior-conditioned auxiliary losses to encourage task-consistent learning and discourage plausible but misleading alternatives. Experiments on AmbiMath, Jigsaw, and MNLI/HANS show that CPS consistently improves over plain and prompt fine-tuning. On AmbiMath, CPS achieves 97.6% average exact-match accuracy. On Jigsaw, CPS improves average Macro F1 by 9.5 percentage points over standard fine-tuning, and with 1/10 of the experimental training data slightly exceeds full-data plain fine-tuning. On HANS, CPS improves non-entailment accuracy by 8.3 and 5.2 percentage points for LLaMA 3.1 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B, respectively, while maintaining comparable in-domain MNLI accuracy. These results support our central claim: task-level natural-language priors can provide useful guidance as auxiliary learning signals for low-resource LLM training. Our code and data will be publicly available.

papers.title: DE-Venus: A Data-Efficient RLVR Framework for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves large language model reasoning, but its practical scaling is constrained by expensive on-policy rollouts and the cost of obtaining reliable targets at scale. Existing methods address sample selection, incomplete supervision, or noisy labels separately, often entangling supervision logic with distributed training and hindering controlled comparison and reuse. We present DE-Venus, a unified framework for data-efficient RLVR that treats supervision as evolving state across data preparation and policy optimization. It organizes this lifecycle into three modules: Active Data Selection allocates training and annotation budgets; Weak Supervision Construction derives learning signals from unlabeled examples; and Training-Time Supervision Refinement filters or corrects unreliable supervision. DE-Venus supports seven representative methods and a data-selection pipeline by expressing method-specific decisions as offline dataset transitions or online transformations of targets, rewards, batches, and advantages while preserving verl's distributed execution contracts. Across public benchmarks and three business scenarios, separate configurations preserve or improve model quality with only 10% of labels or as little as 13% of relevant data; selected business configurations also reduce observed convergence steps by 63%--75%. DE-Venus thus reduces annotation and training costs without sacrificing scalable RL execution.

summary.limitations: 作者指出，对不同 RLVR 算法的系统性比较超出本报告范围。

deep_dive.overview: DE‑Venus 通过将监督视为在准备和优化阶段可变的状态，降低可验证奖励 RL 的成本。它提供三种可互换模块——Active Data Selection（基于不确定性、探针校准）、Weak Supervision Construction（伪目标、基于一致性的奖励）和 Training‑Time Supervision Refinement（奖励动态、几何过滤）。基于 verl 分布式系统实现，保持现有 RLVR 合约，同时将方法特定决策表达为数据集转换或在线转换。 在 DeepMath‑103K 上使用 Qwen3‑8B‑Base 的实验表明，该框架在使用少量标注的情况下，性能可匹配或超越全监督，并显著减少训练步数。

papers.title: BASP: Communication-Efficient Batch-Aware Sequence Parallelism for LLM Training
papers.abstract: Long-context reasoning for large language models (LLMs) is becoming increasingly important, but training over long sequences remains challenging due to massive memory and communication requirements. Sequence parallelism has emerged as an essential technique for addressing bottlenecks in long sequence LLM training. However, we observe that existing sequence parallelism methods are batch-agnostic and apply uniform sequence partitioning across all batch sizes, resulting in inefficient communication. In this paper, we introduce Batch- Aware Sequence Parallelism (BASP), a sequence parallelism approach that leverages batch structure to reduce communication overhead. BASP exploits batch structure by partitioning GPUs into disjoint sequence-parallel groups according to the micro- batch size. This design reduces the all-to-all communication group size, thereby localizing communication and improving training efficiency. Experimental results on an NVIDIA A100 cluster show that BASP improves end-to-end training time by up to 1.17 - 1.31x in Llama and Qwen models compared to standard sequence parallel baselines, while preserving identical model accuracy and memory usage.

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Capture the Diversity in their Training Data?
papers.abstract: Large language models are trained to model conditional distributions over text, yet it remains inadequately understood whether they capture the full diversity of plausible outputs present in their training data. We study this question through an information-theoretic lens by comparing the conditional entropy of model-generated outputs with that of the corresponding training data. Given paired input-output samples, we use conditional entropy and its matrix-based analogue based on von Neumann entropy to measure output variability beyond what is explained by the conditioning input, without requiring multiple reference outputs for the same prompt. Across LLM families with publicly available training data, including OLMo, Pythia, and GPT-Neo, we consistently find that model-generated outputs exhibit lower conditional entropy than their training data, across different model scales, sequence lengths, and decoding strategies. We observe a similar conditional diversity gap beyond language modeling, including class-conditioned ImageNet generators and text-conditioned models trained on MS-COCO. To address this gap, we propose a post-hoc correction mechanism that generates multiple outputs for each input and reweights them through a matrix-entropy projection, increasing conditional diversity while remaining close to the original model distribution. We prove the concavity of the matrix-based conditional entropy functional, which makes the resulting entropy-constrained projection a convex optimization problem, and develop a scalable mirror-descent algorithm for its implementation. Our results reveal a systematic conditional diversity gap between modern generative models and their training data, and provide an information-theoretic framework for measuring and mitigating this gap.

summary.method: 通过矩阵形式的 von Neumann 熵测量条件熵，并使用凸熵投影（通过镜像下降求解）对多个生成候选进行重新加权。
summary.limitations: 该方法为后置，需为每个 prompt 生成大量候选，仅使用基于熵的指标进行评估。
summary.problem: 大型语言模型是否能够捕获给定 prompt 条件下的全部合理输出。
summary.takeaway: LLM 系统性地低估训练数据中的条件输出多样性，但后置的熵约束重新加权可恢复多样性。
summary.why_for_you: 提供信息论工具评估与提升数据多样性，适用于数据选择和鲁棒对抗训练。
summary.evidence: 在 OLMo、Pythia 和 GPT‑Neo 上，模型输出的指数条件 VNE（如 218.88 对 338.58）在所有解码策略下均低于训练数据。

signals.text: 发现 LLM 中系统性的条件多样性缺口，例如 OLMo 相较训练数据出现 119.70 的 exp.Cond.VNE 差距。
提出基于矩阵熵投影的 convex entropy‑constrained 重新加权，使用可扩展的镜像下降在乘积单纯形上求解。
实证表明，模型生成的输出在所有解码方法下的 exp.Cond.VNE（如 218.88 对 338.58）均低于训练数据。

deep_dive.overview: 本文使用 Shannon 熵和矩阵形式的 von Neumann 熵对 (prompt, continuation) 配对样本量化条件输出多样性，发现 LLM 的续写多样性始终低于训练语料。为此，作者提出对每个 prompt 的多个候选进行后置熵约束凸投影重新加权，采用可扩展的镜像下降算法保持 prompt 边缘分布。实验覆盖三大开源 LLM 系列和若干条件图像生成器，验证了该缺口并展示重新加权提升条件熵的效果。

methodology.title: Conditional entropy 测量

methodology.title: Entropy‑constrained 重加权
methodology.detail: 对每个 prompt 生成 m 个候选，然后求解一个凸优化，使 matrix‑based 条件熵最大化，同时保持 prompt 边际，使用在 simplex 笛卡尔积上的 mirror‑descent 并结合 sketch 的联合特征。

mechanism.title: matrix‑based 熵的凸性

contributions: 使用 conditional entropy 和 matrix‑based von Neumann entropy 的条件多样性评估公式。
在文本和图像 generative models 中实证发现一致的 conditional diversity 差距。
对 matrix‑based conditional entropy 函数的凹性提供理论证明。
用于 entropy‑constrained reweighting 的可扩展 mirror‑descent 算法，采用 sketched joint features。
limitations: 后置方法需要为每个提示生成多个候选，导致推理成本上升。

papers.title: SEAL: Reinforcing Global Safety in Mixture-of-Experts through Shared Expert ALignment
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a scaling architecture for large language models that activates only a small subset of expert modules per token, enabling massive parameter growth with nearly constant computation. Recent Hybrid MoE architecture adds \textit{shared experts} to capture consistently useful representations, further improving stability and generalization. MoE now powers many flagship open-source and commercial models, yet remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Specifically, sparse routing introduces a structural vulnerability: MoE safety hinges on which experts are activated, and adversaries can subvert this selection through jailbreak prompts, malicious fine-tuning, and weight-level pruning of safety-critical neurons. Existing defenses primarily focus on hardening the router, but an adversary may still manipulate or bypass the routing trajectory due to the routing process's nondeterministic nature, thereby collapsing the defense. To cope with this problem, we first identify theoretically and empirically that shared expert, an always-activated component containing a small proportion of safety-critical neurons, can overcome the uncertainty of sparsely activated routing path and serve as a router-independent anchor to enhance global safety alignment. Based on this insight, we propose SEAL, a training-time parameter-efficient defense that produces a plug-and-play adapter attached to shared expert, and SEAL++, a variant that adds an orthogonal constraint preserving pre-existing safety subspaces during training. We evaluate SEAL and SEAL++ across six attack scenarios that combine three adversarial inputs (harmful prompting, jailbreak, malicious fine-tuning) with and without neuron pruning. SEAL reduces attack success rate (ASR) by up to 60\%, at a capability cost of at most 1.4\% on a five-benchmark average. Additionally, SEAL can seamlessly integrate with router-level ......

summary.takeaway: SEAL and SEAL++ add a lightweight adapter to shared experts, providing a router‑independent safety anchor for hybrid MoE LLMs.
summary.problem: Sparse routing in Mixture‑of‑Experts models lets adversaries bypass safety by manipulating expert selection, fine‑tuning, or pruning.
summary.method: SEAL trains a parameter‑efficient plug‑and‑play adapter on shared experts, while SEAL++ adds an orthogonal constraint to preserve existing safety subspaces.
summary.evidence: Across six attack scenarios, SEAL cuts attack success rate by up to 60% with ≤1.4% average capability loss, and combined with router‑level defenses lowers ASR to 4.8% (≈5× improvement).
summary.limitations: Evaluation is limited to four hybrid MoE models (14B‑35B) and six predefined attack scenarios.
summary.why_for_you: If you seek efficient adversarial defenses for MoE LLMs, SEAL offers a concrete, low‑overhead method targeting the shared‑expert component.

signals.text: SEAL introduces a shared‑expert‑only adapter that reduces MoE attack success up to 60%.
SEAL++ adds an orthogonal constraint preserving pre‑existing safety subspaces during training.
Combined with router‑level defenses, ASR drops to 4.8%, a >5× reduction, with ≤1.4% capability cost.

deep_dive.overview: The paper identifies the unconditional execution of shared experts as a reliable safety anchor in hybrid Mixture‑of‑Experts LLMs. Building on this insight, SEAL trains a lightweight adapter attached solely to shared experts, and SEAL++ further enforces orthogonal preservation of safety subspaces. Experiments on four diverse MoE models (14B‑35B) under six attack configurations—prompt injection, jailbreak, malicious fine‑tuning, each with/without neuron pruning—show substantial ASR reductions while incurring minimal performance loss. The approach integrates seamlessly with existing router‑level defenses.

methodology.title: SEAL adapter training
methodology.detail: A parameter‑efficient plug‑and‑play module is inserted into each shared expert and trained with DPO on the PKU‑SafeRLHF dataset, leaving routed experts frozen.

methodology.title: SEAL++ orthogonal constraint
methodology.detail: During adapter training, an orthogonal regularizer enforces that updates remain orthogonal to the subspace spanned by pre‑existing safety neurons, preserving prior safety alignment.

mechanism.title: Unconditional execution guarantee
mechanism.detail: Shared experts run on every token regardless of routing, ensuring safety‑critical neurons are always active even if the router is compromised.

mechanism.title: Attack surface reduction
mechanism.detail: Because safety resides in a component that cannot be bypassed, adversaries must target the always‑executed shared experts, raising the effort required for successful attacks.

experiments.title: Model and attack setup
experiments.detail: Four hybrid MoE models (Qwen1.5‑MoE, DeepSeek‑MoE, GLM‑4.7‑Flash, Qwen3.5‑30B) spanning 14B‑35B parameters and 1‑2 shared experts were evaluated. Six attack scenarios combined three adversarial inputs (harmful prompting, jailbreak, malicious fine‑tuning) with/without neuron pruning. Safety responses were classified by GPT‑5‑nano with 98.1% inter‑run agreement.

experiments.title: Metrics
experiments.detail: Attack Success Rate (ASR) measured as worst‑case across conditions; capability cost measured as average performance drop on five downstream benchmarks.

findings.title: SEAL effectiveness
findings.detail: SEAL reduces ASR by up to 60% while incurring at most 1.4% average capability loss across the five‑benchmark suite.

findings.title: Synergy with router defenses
findings.detail: When combined with a router‑level defense, overall ASR falls to 4.8%, more than five times lower than router defense alone.

findings.title: Safety neuron preservation
findings.detail: Models with concentrated shared‑expert safety encoding (Qwen1.5, DeepSeek) retain >80% of safety neuron identity after SEAL training, indicating minimal subspace drift.

contributions: Identification of shared experts as a router‑independent safety anchor.
SEAL: a plug‑and‑play adapter for shared experts that improves MoE safety.
SEAL++: orthogonal regularization to preserve existing safety subspaces.
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple MoE architectures and attack vectors.
limitations: Experiments cover only four hybrid MoE models up to 35B parameters.
Evaluation limited to six predefined attack scenarios; broader threat models not explored.
open_questions: How does shared‑expert augmentation scale to trillion‑parameter MoE systems?
Can adaptive adversaries learn to circumvent the shared‑expert safety anchor?
What are the interactions between SEAL and other alignment techniques such as RLHF or instruction tuning?

papers.title: How Perturbations Propagate: A Multi-Level Analysis of Robustness in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Language models encounter typos, corrupted text, altered words, and disrupted token order, yet robustness is usually evaluated only through output behavior. We study how six naturalistic and synthetic input perturbations propagate through decoder-only language models at three levels: output behavior, hidden-state geometry, and attention-head function. We evaluate behavioral effects across four GPT-2 and two Qwen2.5 checkpoints by analyzing layerwise geometry using centered kernel alignment and intrinsic dimension, and examine attention-head responses in GPT-2. Perturbation types produce distinguishable metric profiles that are not fully captured by output measures and are only partly consistent across the tested checkpoints. Copying scores are especially associated with activation-patching recovery under token substitution and shuffling. Gradient-guided HotFlip perturbations also cause stronger behavioral and representational disruption than rate-matched random token substitutions in GPT-2; their behavioral effects are consistent across all six tested checkpoints. Our results show that robustness claims based on a single behavioral or representational metric can be misleading, and motivate multi-level evaluation of how perturbations alter language-model computation.

papers.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) combines student-generated rollouts with dense token-level supervision from a teacher. Existing work has mainly studied its algorithmic behavior, leaving the role of training data unclear. We examine this role at the data-minimal limit by training on a single query. One-shot OPD keeps improving for hundreds of steps and recovers most of full-data OPD's gain across task domains and model families. We explain this result through the states visited during training and the rate at which the student aligns with the teacher. We measure \emph{state coverage}, the fraction of the states full-data OPD visits that a query set's rollouts reach. A single query already reaches \(71.5\%\), most of it within the first 100 steps. Adding semantically distinct queries raises coverage and validation accuracy together, until 16 queries reach \(98.9\%\) and match full-data training. Yet alignment slows at a similar pace whether OPD trains on one query or the whole dataset, and even a fixed set of states takes hundreds of steps to absorb. OPD is therefore data-overfed but algorithm-starved. Its rollouts quickly expose broad supervision, while the student absorbs that supervision increasingly slowly. The state-coverage result extends to multi-teacher OPD, where 16 semantically diverse queries per domain match full-data MOPD. As a further stress test, content-light templates and off-domain WildChat queries also approach the real-query baseline. Task content and induced state coverage can therefore come apart. We hope these findings direct future work toward the step efficiency of OPD, and prompt a re-examination of the data and the mechanisms behind its recent successes in frontier post-training.

summary.takeaway: 使用单一查询的一次性 on-policy 蒸馏可恢复全数据 OPD 在任务和模型系列中的大部分性能提升。
summary.method: 作者在单一查询（一次性）和小规模语义多样的查询集上训练 OPD，测量 state coverage 与 alignment dynamics。

summary.why_for_you: 鉴于您关注 on-policy 蒸馏和数据选择，该工作表明 state-coverage 指标可用于指导最小查询选择，以实现高效 OPD。

deep_dive.overview: 本文通过将数据集缩减至单查询（一次性 OPD）或小规模语义多样查询集，研究 OPD 实际所需的训练数据量。提出了 state‑coverage 指标，用于量化全数据 OPD 访问的状态中有多少被有限查询的 rollouts 覆盖。四个任务域和三种模型系列的实验表明，单查询已覆盖 71.5% 的状态空间并恢复大部分验证增益，16 个查询则达到 98.9% 覆盖率并完全匹配全数据结果。作者认为 OPD 数据充裕但算法受限，teacher 信号的吸收速率限制了训练时长。

methodology.title: 单次 OPD 训练
methodology.detail: 在单个查询生成的 rollout 上训练 student，最多 1000 步，在每个访问的状态施加密集的 token‑level teacher 监督。

methodology.title: 多教师扩展 (MOPD)

findings.detail: One‑shot OPD 在前 100 步内达到 71.5% 的 state coverage，并在所有领域恢复了大部分 full‑data OPD 的增益。

papers.title: The Dice Roll Method: A Standardized Protocol for Repeated-Query Auditing of Large Language Model Brand Recommendations
papers.abstract: Background: Researchers increasingly use repeated identical prompts to audit stochastic variation in large language model (LLM) brand recommendations, yet no standardized protocol exists for setting iteration counts, selecting stability metrics, or establishing reliability thresholds. Objective: We formalize the Dice Roll Method as a reusable protocol for repeated-query auditing of LLM brand recommendations, grounded in a generative model of temperature-scaled nucleus sampling. Methods: Total response variance is decomposed into sampling, prompt-phrasing, run-to-run, and model-version components. The stack: a negative-binomial mixed model with iterations as repeated measures; Cliff's delta as the distribution-free effect size; dependence-preserving bootstrap; simulation-based power; a generalizability-theory decomposition; drift diagnostics on pinned snapshots. We reanalyse five brand-recommendation auditing studies: approximately 190,000 observations, 270+ brands, 6 languages, iteration counts 5 to 40. Results: Three tiers of iteration guidance emerge from the D-study: exploratory (n = 5, G = 0.58), confirmatory (n = 10, G = 0.74), and rigorous (n = 15, G = 0.81), tied to effect-size and generalizability targets. The four metric families (count, set, embedding, fairness-adjusted PASOR) are complementary, motivating a compact metric battery over single indicators. A pre-registered external validation on three independent corpora (Motoki et al., 100-round; Rozado, 24 models; llm-stability) reproduces the D-study reliability prediction in 37 of 39 cells with no failures and the n = 5 power value to two decimals; the fixed tiers do not transfer, supporting a pilot-then-solve reading. Conclusion: The protocol gives repeated-query auditing of LLM brand recommendations a statistically principled footing under the conditional, non-Gaussian structure of real autoregressive generation.
papers.comment: 30 pages, 2 figures, 19 tables. Substantially revised; supersedes the Research Square preprint 10.21203/rs.3.rs-8883056/v1. Includes a pre-registered external validation on three independent corpora (Motoki et al., Rozado, llm-stability)

papers.title: Knowledge Acquisition During Pre-training? Large Language Models Learn Better With Auxiliary Views
papers.abstract: Gaps remain in our understanding of how large language models (LLMs) acquire knowledge during pre-training. We posit that auxiliary views, reformulations of knowledge, are causally helpful for learning. We design controlled experiments to isolate this. First, we confirm that repetition is necessary for acquisition and clarify that paraphrasing helps only at smaller batch sizes. Second, holding the token budget fixed, allocating tokens from document repetition to auxiliary views improves learning, counterintuitively, even for factual recall. Third, the effectiveness of auxiliary views is not contingent on the strength of the teacher model that generates them. Fourth, we identify forms of knowledge, contextual and foundational, that aid learning in the presence of prior knowledge gaps. Finally, we examine how these effects manifest mechanistically via layer-wise biases and compression. Together, our findings suggest that auxiliary representations of knowledge, which arise naturally in large pre-training corpora, are a key factor in the success of pre-training and offer a plausible explanation for why data diversity matters.

summary.takeaway: 辅助的知识改写提升 LLM 预训练效率和事实回忆。
summary.method: 在固定 token 预算下，将文档重复的 token 重新分配到教师生成的辅助视图（如改写）上。

summary.limitations: 在更大 batch size 时改写收益减弱，实验仅限于 OLMo‑2‑32B。
summary.evidence: 在 OLMo‑2‑32B 上，包含辅助视图的混合训练在事实和推理探测上优于仅源或仅改写的训练。

deep_dive.overview: 作者研究在 LLM 预训练期间如何表征知识。将 auxiliary views 定义为同一知识的多样改写（如博客、问答、教材），并检验将固定 token 预算分配给这些视图而非单纯重复是否提升学习。对 OLMo‑2‑32B 的受控实验比较 source‑only、paraphrase‑only 与 source + auxiliary 三种训练混合。结果表明 auxiliary views 在 factual 与 inference 基准上带来更大提升，收益受 batch size 调节且与 teacher 模型强度无关。机制分析揭示层级偏置转移和压缩效应。

papers.title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous SOC analysts, but two limitations make them unreliable at enterprise scale: a finite context window cannot hold a multi-thousand-host authentication graph, and free-form generation offers no guarantee that a recommended containment action is consistent with the topology it operates on. We present Sentinel-RL, an agentic-SOC architecture that decouples topological reasoning from semantic reasoning: a heterogeneous graph attention encoder summarizes the live authentication subgraph into a fixed-dimensional state, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy maps this state to a constrained set of investigative actions, and an LLM agent loop is restricted to consuming the policy's recommendations and producing analyst-readable narratives gated by a critic. We instantiate the system on the LANL Comprehensive, Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events dataset and the Indiana University Quartz HPC cluster, reporting four results: (i) a two-phase CREATE ingestion pattern loads a 24M-edge authentication subgraph into Neo4j in 14.2 minutes on a single 32-core node, roughly 24x faster than the canonical MERGE-based pipeline; (ii) a sliding-window alert engine reliably trips a 25-event/10-second threshold in <=2.5 s across 50 trials; (iii) PPO training over 200 iterations converges to a mean episodic return of 8.74+/-0.31, with held-out precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.87 on labeled red-team events; and (iv) the integrated containment loop completes a full detect-investigate-recommend-human-approve cycle in a median of 6.3 s. We contribute a reusable engineering pattern (the hot-node deadlock workaround), a portable HPC deployment pattern (anchor-node co-location), and an enterprise-readiness analysis covering false-positive economics, reversibility guarantees, audit compliance, and the human-approval boundary.

papers.title: Epistemic Warrant for LLM Recommendations: Characterizing the Basis for Reliance When Ground Truth Is Unavailable
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to support organizational decisions, yet users often lack a principled basis for assessing whether to rely on a specific recommendation. Existing approaches typically evaluate broad model properties, such as reliability, uncertainty, or robustness, or focus on user trust, rather than the underlying basis for relying on an individual recommendation. Adapting theoretical foundations from epistemology, we introduce epistemic warrant, a decision-level construct that characterizes the stability of a model's preference and the scope over which that preference holds. We operationalize this construct through a four-tier reliance certificate for pairwise recommendations, distinguishing among unstable, context-dependent, locally supported, and broadly supported recommendations. We validate the construct using contemporary methodologies: known-groups tests successfully recover expert-prespecified warrant orderings, and stronger warrants systematically align with independent consensus from crowd workers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that epistemic warrant provides information distinct from verbalized confidence and is not readily explained by decision difficulty. Ultimately, this framework offers a theoretically grounded, implementable approach for characterizing the warrant of individual LLM recommendations when objective ground truth is unavailable.

summary.takeaway: Adapting theoretical foundations from epistemology, we introduce epistemic warrant, a decision-level construct that characterizes the stability of a model's preference and the scope over which that preference holds.

papers.title: LLM4CKD: Large Language Models for Early Stage Chronic Kidney Disease Screening
papers.abstract: Early screening of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is critical for timely intervention, yet most machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches require labeled data and model training, limiting their use in real-world screening settings. This study evaluates the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) for CKD screening under zero-shot and few-shot in-context learning settings and compares them with traditional ML and DL methods. We propose a framework that uses clinically selected tabular features and structured prompt templates to enable LLM-based inference without task-specific training. LLM performance is evaluated across multiple prompt styles, feature configurations, and data settings, and compared with standard ML, DL, and tabular foundation model (TFM) baselines, and existing CKD screening tools. The results show that LLMs can achieve competitive performance using only a small number of examples, often matching or outperforming traditional approaches in low-data settings. However, their performance remains model-dependent and less stable as input complexity increases. In contrast, ML, DL, and TFM models show more consistent improvement with larger training data. Overall, the findings highlight a trade-off between data efficiency and stability, suggesting that LLMs may serve as a flexible complementary approach for CKD screening when labeled data are limited.

papers.title: DKL: Decoupled Knowledge Learning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models
papers.abstract: RAG has become the de facto method for incorporating new, corpus-specific knowledge into an instruction following LLM (Instruct LLM). Although RAG-based prompting improves factual grounding, it fails when retrieval is incorrect or incomplete, leading to hallucinations. Finetuning methods such as RAFT and PA-RAG enhance RAG by injecting new knowledge into the model's parameters, but require generating a massive amount of synthetic QA that covers the entire corpus. Extended Pre-Training (EPT) on the text corpus avoids the need for comprehensive synthetic data generation but compromises an Instruct LLM's instruction-following capabilities, necessitating instruction fine-tuning (IFT) after pre-training. However, IFT is costly and may be infeasible due to the unavailability of an instruction-tuning corpus. In this work, we propose DKL-Decoupled Knowledge Learning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models. Instead of doing EPT on the Instruct LLM, DKL performs EPT on its corresponding base LLM to infuse new knowledge. These knowledge infused weights are then merged with the Instruct LLM, imparting new knowledge without affecting their instruction-following capabilities. DKL is a lightweight method that avoids expensive instruction fine-tuning and relies on model merging to infuse the new knowledge into the Instruct LLM without destroying its instruction following capabilities. Empirical results show that DKL improves RAG accuracy from 54.17 to 79.26 on retrieval failure cases, while outperforming prior approaches with substantially less training data.

summary.takeaway: In this work, we propose DKL-Decoupled Knowledge Learning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models.

summary.method: In this work, we propose DKL-Decoupled Knowledge Learning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models.

papers.title: From Reweighting to Rewriting: Unlocking the Intervention Effects of Influential Samples in Training Data Attribution
papers.abstract: Training data attribution (TDA) aims to identify training examples that shape model behavior, but its intervention value depends on both which examples are selected and how they are modified. Influence functions (IF) estimate behavioral changes under infinitesimal reweighting, yet IF-selected examples often show limited advantages over random selection under conventional weight-based interventions. This raises the question of whether influential examples lack intervention value or whether reweighting fails to realize their behavioral leverage.We introduce influence-guided response rewriting, which uses IF to identify intervention targets and replaces their responses with behavior-aligned or behavior-opposed supervision while keeping instructions fixed. Across four open-weight LLMs, we compare rewriting and reweighting on the same influence-selected examples using epistemic abstention as our primary testbed. Response rewriting produces stronger, more persistent, and bidirectional behavioral shifts, while reweighting the same examples yields weak and inconsistent effects. Further analyses show that influence-selected examples provide greater rewriting leverage than alternative selectors, with changes remaining concentrated on target-relevant behaviors. The same qualitative contrast extends to safety refusal. These results distinguish the local reweighting effects captured by influence estimates from the broader intervention leverage of the examples they identify, motivating intervention-aware evaluation of TDA methods.

summary.limitations: 评估仅限于 supervised fine‑tuning、四个模型和 abstention/safety 基准，未检验更广泛的泛化能力。
summary.evidence: 在四个 open‑weight LLMs 中，重写相较于删除或上调相同样本，能够在 epistemic abstention 和 safety refusal 上产生更强、更稳健、双向的变化。
summary.problem: 基于权重的对 influence‑selected 示例的干预相较随机选择优势有限，质疑其实用性。
summary.takeaway: influence‑guided response rewriting 相较于 reweighting，对有影响力的训练样本提供更有效且持久的行为干预。
summary.method: 通过 influence functions 选择高影响力样本，并在保持指令不变的情况下，用 behavior‑aligned 或相反的模板替换其响应。
summary.why_for_you: 契合您对数据选择和高效对抗训练的兴趣，展示了一种更有力利用 influential examples 的方法。

signals.text: 引入 influence‑guided response rewriting 作为一种新 TDA 干预，优于 reweighting。
使用 influence functions 选取样本，然后仅通过 template pools 中的固定提示重写响应。
在四个 LLMs 上展示了针对 abstention 和 safety 的更强、持久、双向行为变化，但仅限于这些任务。

deep_dive.overview: 本文研究了为何 influence‑function (IF) 选取的示例在传统 reweighting 下常未能提升模型行为。提出一种解耦框架：IF 确定高杠杆训练点，response rewriting 仅修改响应且保持指令不变，使用 behavior‑aligned 或相反的模板。对四个 open‑weight LLMs 的实证研究表明，与删除或上调相同示例相比，rewriting 能显著产生更强、更稳健且双向的 epistemic abstention 和 safety refusal 变化。分析显示，influential 示例蕴含潜在杠杆，rewriting 可在不削弱整体能力的前提下加以释放。

mechanism.detail: 重写会改变与有影响力示例相关的监督信号，直接引导模型向目标行为靠近或远离，同时保持提示不变。
mechanism.title: 通过监督信号重定向实现杠杆效应

mechanism.detail: 由于仅修改了响应，重写后的示例继续影响相同的输入分布，将干预集中在目标行为上，而不会造成广泛的能力损失。
mechanism.title: 目标特异性保持

methodology.detail: 为每个SFT训练示例计算IF分数，根据目标行为查询集对示例进行排序，从最有帮助（正分数）到最有害（负分数）。
methodology.title: 影响函数评分

methodology.detail: 将选定示例的原始响应替换为三个模板池中的固定字符串（abstention-refuse, safety-refuse, comply），同时保留原始指令。
methodology.title: 响应重写

methodology.detail: 在修改后的数据集上对基础LLM进行微调，使用相同的SFT配方和超参数，适用于不同模型规模（OLMo2-1B/7B, Qwen3.5-2B, Gemma3-4B）。
methodology.title: 微调设置

experiments.title: 模型与干预比较
experiments.detail: 在同一 IF‑selected 集合上，对四种开放权重 LLM 进行四种干预的评估：删除、加权、行为对齐重写和行为对立重写。

experiments.title: 评估方案
experiments.detail: 主要测试平台是使用来自 CoCoNot、SelfAware 和 KUQ 的 300 道题目的认知回避；安全拒绝通过独立安全基准进行评估。指标包括回避率变化和召回率差异。

experiments.title: 基线与对照
experiments.detail: 随机选择、基于探测的选择和基于投影的选择（高不可回答性）作为基线；所有干预在样本数量上保持一致。

findings.title: 重写优于加权
findings.detail: 相较于对相同 IF‑selected 示例的删除或加权，响应重写在回避和安全行为上产生更强、更稳健且双向的变化。

findings.title: 影响选择示例具有更高杠杆效应
findings.detail: 与基于投影或其他选择器基线相比，影响选择的样本在对齐重写下产生更大效应，在对立重写下产生相当效应。

findings.title: 目标聚焦的变化且不削弱能力
findings.detail: 分析表明，重写效应仍集中于目标行为，并未明显损害整体模型性能。

contributions: 基于 Influence‑guided 的 response rewriting 框架，将 example selection 与 intervention design 解耦。
实证表明，influential examples 包含通过 rewriting 解锁的隐藏 behavioral leverage。
阐述 rewriting 有效原因及其相对于其他 selectors 的适用范围。
limitations: 研究仅限于 supervised fine‑tuning 环境，未在 pre‑training 或 instruction‑tuning 流程中评估。
实验仅覆盖四个 open‑weight LLM 和两个 behavioral domains（abstention、safety refusal）。
rewriting 依赖手工构建的 template pools，可能无法推广至 arbitrary behaviors。
open_questions: Influence‑guided rewriting 能否扩展至更大的 closed‑source 模型和更丰富的 behavioral targets？
有哪些 automated methods 能在超出 fixed templates 的情况下生成有效的 rewrite 内容？
rewriting 对 downstream task performance 与整体 model alignment 的长期影响如何？

papers.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for large language model (LLM) post-training, but its reliance on coarse outcome rewards leads to limited guidance on intermediate reasoning processes. Existing approaches such as process reward modeling and on-policy distillation introduce additional constraints, such as reliance on a specialized reward model or assuming identical reasoning patterns between teacher and student. Nevertheless, we observe that once a reasoning process first goes wrong, evaluating the subsequent reasoning provides limited additional information, as it is already conditioned on an invalid prefix. Therefore, we propose Cliff, a reward shaping strategy that utilizes an off-the-shelf LLM as a teacher to identify the first mistake in each rollout. As a result, the rollout is naturally decomposed into two parts: a correct prefix and an incorrect suffix. Cliff then converts this signal into token-level advantages, assigning positive advantages for the correct prefix and negative feedback afterward. Experiments across 12 different scenarios demonstrate that Cliff consistently improves reasoning performance, outperforming on-policy distillation by 15% and standard GRPO by 7%, even with teachers of modest capability. Furthermore, we analyse the role of ``ground truth'' in Cliff and investigate its training dynamics. These results establish Cliff as a simple, general and effective approach for improving RLVR with richer, fine-grained supervision.

summary.limitations: 该方法依赖能够准确识别首个错误的 teacher，若缺少 ground‑truth filter，较弱的 teacher 将出现更大的性能下降。
summary.evidence: 在 12 种场景中，Cliff 相比 on‑policy distillation 提升 15%，相比 GRPO 提升 7%，对强 teacher 移除 ground‑truth filtering 时仅下降约 2%。
summary.problem: RLVR 中的 outcome‑only rewards 反馈稀疏，无法对中间推理步骤进行奖励。
summary.takeaway: Cliff 通过奖励至首个推理错误的方式，为 RLVR 添加细粒度的过程监督。
summary.method: Cliff 使用 off‑the‑shelf LLM teacher 定位 rollout 中的首个错误，并在其之前分配正向 token advantage，之后分配负向 advantage。
summary.why_for_you: 如果您从事 on‑policy distillation 或高效对抗训练，Cliff 提供一种简洁、信号更强的替代方案，可提升 RLVR 性能。

signals.text: Cliff 在 12 项任务上相较 on‑policy distillation 提升 15% 推理性能。
Cliff 使用 LLM teacher 找到首个错误，并将 rollout 划分以进行 token 级别的 advantage 分配。
对强 teacher 若无 ground‑truth filter，性能下降约 2%，对弱 teacher 则更大。

deep_dive.overview: Cliff 通过引入首个推理错误的位置这一粗粒度但信息丰富的过程信号，缓解 RLVR 中 outcome‑only rewards 的稀疏性。off‑the‑shelf LLM teacher 对每个学生 rollout 进行评判，标记最早的错误。随后将 rollout 划分为正确前缀和错误后缀，并相应分配 token 级别的 advantage。结合 Group Relative Policy Optimization，该方案在十二个推理基准上实现稳定提升，超越 on‑policy distillation 与标准 GRPO，且保持模型无关性。

mechanism.detail: 仅识别第一个错误即可提供足够的指导，因为后续推理基于已无效的前缀，类似于空虚蕴含。
mechanism.title: 粗粒度过程监督

mechanism.detail: 由于推迟错误总是产生更高的优势，奖励无法通过后期标记的简单操作被操纵。
mechanism.title: 奖励劫持抵抗

methodology.detail: 教师LLM评估学生轨迹并返回最早错误推理步骤（Pitfall Step）的索引。
methodology.title: 首次错误检测

methodology.detail: Pitfall Step之前的标记获得更高的（正向）优势分数；之后的标记获得负分数，这与GRPO类似，但使用了分割信号。
methodology.title: 优势塑造

methodology.detail: Cliff基于Group Relative Policy Optimization目标，用双段优势向量替代了统一轨迹优势。
methodology.title: 与GRPO的集成

experiments.title: 基准套件
experiments.detail: 使用了十二个推理场景（包括 GSM8k、MATH‑500、DAPO、AIME）；一个包含 50 条正确和 50 条错误回滚的人类标注子集用于评估评审质量。

experiments.title: 教师模型
experiments.detail: 评估了 Qwen3‑32B、Gemma3‑27B 和一款 SOTA 模型；表 1 报告了参考解答准确率（65–93%）、评审准确率（88–100%）以及与人工标注的平均 Pitfall‑step 距离。

experiments.title: 基线与指标
experiments.detail: 与 on‑policy distillation（OPD）和标准 GRPO 进行比较；改进以最终推理准确率的百分比提升来衡量。

experiments.title: 消融研究
experiments.detail: 将教师从双重 credit assignment 中剥离仅带来微小提升，证实 first‑mistake split 是性能的主要驱动因素。

experiments.title: 真实标签过滤器分析
experiments.detail: 去除过滤教师参考解答的 verifier 导致强教师（Qwen3‑4B、SOTA）准确率下降约 2%，而弱教师（Gemma3‑27B）下降至 2–3%。

findings.title: 性能提升
findings.detail: Cliff 在十二个任务上平均比 OPD 高出 15%，比 GRPO 高出 7%。

findings.title: 教师可靠性
findings.detail: 教师更高的问题求解准确率与更一致的 Pitfall‑step 识别相关（例如，SOTA 模型参考准确率 93%，误报为 0）。

findings.title: Credit assignment 重要性
findings.detail: 消融实验表明，仅将教师用作 reward model 只能带来小幅提升，而显式的 prefix‑suffix advantage assignment 则推动了大部分改进。

contributions: First‑mistake based reward shaping for RLVR

papers.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
papers.abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is a critical task in telecom network operations, but diagnosing performance degradations in modern 5G and emerging 6G networks remains challenging due to complex cross-layer dependencies. While large language models (LLMs) offer promising capabilities for reasoning and knowledge integration, directly applying vanilla LLMs to telecom RCA often leads to hallucination, unstable reasoning, and poor alignment with structured network evidence. This work first reviews the evolution of telecom RCA from rule-based and machine learning (ML) approaches to emerging LLM-enabled techniques, and provides an overview of recent paradigms, including structured reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge grounding, agentic orchestration, and verifiable reasoning. Building upon these insights, we propose a structured reasoning framework for LLM-enabled telecom RCA that aligns diagnostic reasoning with telecom-specific evidence and domain knowledge. The proposed approach first organizes heterogeneous network telemetry into canonical contexts, and then enforces decision-path reasoning during diagnosis, and finally generates evidence-grounded explanations for reliable fault identification. Experimental results on two 5G RCA datasets, TeleLogs and TelecomTS, demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves diagnostic accuracy and decision consistency compared with baseline techniques. These cross-dataset results highlight the importance of structured reasoning design for practical LLM-based RCA systems in next-generation telecom networks.

papers.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
papers.abstract: Competitive programming has become a key test of large language model reasoning, with international competitions such as IOI and ICPC representing its most challenging settings. We present an end-to-end specialization pipeline combining large-scale problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL). Using 22,000 curated problems, we train Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (30B-A3B) with SFT and RL and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (550B-A55B) with SFT alone. We further introduce GenCorrect, a feedback-driven test-time compute strategy that iteratively generates, evaluates, and refines diverse solutions. On IOI 2025, Nano-CC improves from 130 points to 291 after post-training and to 468 with GenCorrect, exceeding the gold threshold of 438.3 while Ultra-CC reaches 502. Guided by these results, we develop a competition-specific Ultra-CC system and evaluate it prospectively during IOI 2026. Under the same time, internet-access, and submission constraints as human contestants, it scores 535.4 out of 600, exceeding both the gold threshold of 361.12 and the top human score of 498.27. To our knowledge, this is the first AI system to outscore the highest-scoring human contestant on an IOI problem set.

papers.title: Incremental Pooled LLM Evaluation for Cost-Effective Retrieval Model Selection
papers.abstract: Selecting a retrieval model for a production RAG system requires reliable comparative evaluation, but obtaining relevance judgments at scale is expensive and difficult to repeat as new candidate systems arrive. We study pooled LLM evaluation, in which an LLM judges the union of documents retrieved by the current set of candidate systems, and the pool is then expanded incrementally as new systems are introduced by judging only the new documents they contribute. These judgments are reused to evaluate all systems on a common basis. We validate this approach on four retrieval benchmarks with 11 systems spanning dense, sparse, and hybrid configurations, and deploy it to compare 62 retrieval configurations for a financial news QA system. Pooled LLM rankings correlate strongly with gold-standard evaluation across datasets, and 97% of pairwise system orderings are preserved once bootstrap uncertainty in the qrels is taken into account. In production, document overlap yields 65-80% judgment reuse and up to 4.9x lower evaluation cost, allowing teams to benchmark new retrieval candidates without re-judging previously assessed documents. These results suggest pooled LLM evaluation is a practical and cost-effective workflow for incremental retrieval model selection in deployed systems.

papers.title: Can LLMs Design Video Coding Tools? A Case Study on Planar Mode
papers.abstract: This paper explores whether large language models (LLMs) can design video coding tools, a highly challenging task due to the intricate algorithmic coupling of tool modifications. In particular, we present an empirical case study on the Planar mode, a long-standing intra prediction tool in video coding standards. Our experiments operate within a generation-and-evaluation loop, with the LLM generating new Planar predictors, encoder trials evaluating their coding performance, and the LLM re-generating refined implementations based on the evaluation feedback. We first examine directly replacing the default Planar mode in the Fraunhofer Versatile Video Encoder (VVenC) under its faster preset. Experimental results demonstrate that the LLM-generated mode can outperform the conventional Planar mode on this lightweight toolset, achieving 0.18% bitrate savings with 0.4% complexity overhead on the standard benchmark. We further extend our evaluation to the Enhanced Compression Model (ECM). Leveraging newly introduced directional Planar modes, we investigate two integration strategies: directly replacing them, and introducing the LLM-generated predictor as an additional prediction mode with new syntax elements. The empirical results suggest that both strategies can yield coding gains under a constrained low-resolution setting. Overall, this study offers preliminary evidence and practical insights, highlighting both the potential and open challenges of LLM-based coding tool design.

papers.title: From Rollouts to Recipes: Self-Contained Post-Training for LLMs
papers.abstract: Post-training large language models usually applies a single training recipe to all samples, even though the model's own rollouts reveal different sample-level learning states. We propose Self-Routing, a behavior-conditioned post-training framework that uses rollout correctness and confidence to decide how each sample should be optimized. Depending on its behavior state, a sample is routed to GRPO, on-policy self-distillation, regularization, or skipping, allowing training to adapt without external teachers, extra annotations, or additional sampling. Experiments on mathematical reasoning across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 backbones show that Self-Routing consistently improves over uniform GRPO, uniform OPSD, fixed mixtures, and simpler routing baselines. Further analyses show that the routing distribution changes over training and reduces unnecessary updates on low-signal or already stable samples.

summary.problem: 全局后训练配方忽视了通过 on‑policy rollouts 揭示的样本级学习状态的异质性。

summary.limitations: Self‑Routing 的计算开销高于 Naive‑OPSD，且在最小模型上因自生成信号不稳定而收益不一。

papers.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Benign fine-tuning severely weakens the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs), so we study why refusal behavior is so fragile. While prior work often attributes this failure to gradient conflict, we propose a fundamentally different Fisher-geometric explanation: safety Fisher is low-rank, and alignment makes the safety geometry flatter while preserving an output-routing pathway. After 100 benign fine-tuning examples, this pathway is selectively re-sharpened in output-side MLP modules, explaining the asymmetric fragility: safety can collapse to high attack success rates, while general utility degrades mildly. The routing view also explains why few safety examples can restore refusal behavior, indicating that internal safety-relevant representations are preserved. Finally, we show that LoRA and ASAM mitigate early collapse by suppressing output-side sharpness, but their protection weakens at larger fine-tuning scales. Overall, safety failure is best understood as a disruption of a low-rank output-routing mechanism
papers.comment: Accepted to the Findings of EMNLP 2026

summary.evidence: Safety Fisher sharpness increases 11.2× in output MLPs after 100 benign examples, while utility sharpness only 1.2×.

papers.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
papers.abstract: AI tutors are most useful when they adapt to each student's strengths, weaknesses, and preferred guidance, but evidence about which guidance works for which student is sparse, slow, and costly to collect from real learners. Student simulators can provide this signal as a proxy, yet existing approaches are limited: state-tracking models fit student behavior but struggle to process explanations or corrections, while LLM role-play follows guidance fluently but does not reliably match the competence of the student being imitated. We present StudentSim, a training framework that turns sparse per-student data into individualized simulators through pooled training followed by per-student specialization. The resulting simulators both mirror a student's own responses and update them under tutor guidance. We also introduce StudentSimEval, a standardized protocol covering 60 students across chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics, using public learner datasets with de-identified records shared for research. StudentSimEval measures behavioral fidelity (F), or how well a simulator matches a student's responses, and guidance responsiveness (R), or how readily it updates under tutor guidance, with all methods fit and evaluated on the same records. Across all three domains, StudentSim outperforms GPT-5.4 on both metrics. In chess, StudentSim reaches F=0.51 and R=0.91, compared with 0.23 and 0.72 for GPT-5.4 and 0.45 and 0.27 for Maia2. As a proof of concept, using StudentSim as a reward model for tutor reinforcement learning produces a chess tutor that expert humans rate as more accurate, better-guided, and more personalized than a no-RL baseline and a tutor trained against a GPT-5.4 simulator reward. Code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/StudentSim.

summary.problem: 现有学生模拟器要么仅跟踪行为而不处理教师解释，要么在引导下角色扮演但无法匹配个体能力。
summary.method: StudentSim 在汇总的学生数据上训练共享 LLM，然后通过 LoRA 微调为每个学生专化，保持统一架构。
summary.limitations: 评估仅覆盖三类任务和 60 名学生，且框架未建模长期学习动态。
summary.evidence: 在 StudentSimEval 基准上，StudentSim 在棋类任务中达到 F=0.51、R=0.91，超越 GPT‑5.4 (F=0.23, R=0.72) 与 Maia2 (F=0.45, R=0.27)。
summary.takeaway: StudentSim 的两阶段微调生成的每学生 LLM 模拟器显著提升了对真实学生回答的忠实度和对教师引导的响应性。
summary.why_for_you: 其高效的每学生适配符合您对 LLM 损失曲面分析以实现个性化、低成本训练的兴趣。

deep_dive.overview: StudentSim 通过两阶段训练弥合状态跟踪模型（高忠实度、低引导处理）与 LLM 角色扮演（高引导处理、低忠实度）之间的差距。第一阶段在汇总的学习者数据上微调基础 LLM，获取通用任务知识；第二阶段为每位学习者添加轻量 LoRA 专化，使模型适应其回答模式并仍能接受教师纠正。作者在覆盖棋类、二语英语写作和数学的标准基准 StudentSimEval 上评估，测量行为忠实度和引导响应性。

findings.title: 更高的忠实度与响应性
findings.detail: StudentSim 在棋类任务中达到 F=0.51、R=0.91，优于 GPT‑5.4 (F=0.23, R=0.72) 与 Maia2 (F=0.45, R=0.27)；在 L2 与数学领域也有类似提升。将 StudentSim 作为奖励模型用于 RL 教师训练，可得到的棋类教师被专家评为更准确、引导更好、个性化程度更高，胜过使用 GPT‑5.4 或未使用 RL 的教师。

contributions: 一种两阶段先汇总后专化的训练框架，用于每学生 LLM 模拟器，联合优化行为忠实度和引导响应性。

methodology.title: 两阶段训练
