papers.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Policy optimization (PO) for Large Language Models faces a stability--exploration trade-off, currently mediated by an action-side Policy-KL regularizer. This puts practitioners in a double bind: keeping Policy-KL constrains response behavior and consumes the action-side exploration budget, while dropping it leaves the optimization without an explicit drift control. We argue for an alternative that breaks the dilemma by moving regularization to the input side. As training progresses, the distribution over training queries induced by the current policy drifts unchecked from its pre-RL reference distribution. Concretely, Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) introduces a Query-KL (QKL) term that bounds this query distribution shift, together with a dataset-static reference-derived per-query weight that biases each per-query update toward queries typical under the reference. The QKL gradient flows strictly through the query likelihood; the response score function used by policy-gradient estimators does not appear in the QKL term, so QKL exerts no direct gradient pressure on the response distribution---exploration is preserved. ERPO plugs into GRPO/PPO/REINFORCE-style pipelines without additional forward passes. On six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, ERPO replaces the standard Policy-KL regularizer while achieving effective control over query distribution drift, delivering stronger accuracy and substantially more stable behavior under high-temperature decoding and long-horizon training.Our source code are available at https://github.com/alibaba/ERPO

summary.takeaway: ERPO replaces the action‑side Policy‑KL with a query‑side KL regularizer, yielding more stable and accurate LLM policy optimization.
summary.problem: LLM policy optimization faces a stability–exploration dilemma because the model‑induced query distribution drifts unchecked during training.
summary.method: ERPO adds a Query‑KL penalty between the current policy’s query distribution and a pre‑RL reference, plus a static per‑query weight, without influencing response‑side gradients.
summary.evidence: On six mathematical reasoning benchmarks ERPO improves Avg@32 by up to 14.9% (6.2% average) and shows reduced query‑KL growth, indicating greater stability.
summary.limitations: The alignment‑preserving assumption is only empirically validated on mathematical reasoning tasks, and broader applicability is not demonstrated.
summary.why_for_you: The query‑distribution regularization directly addresses loss‑landscape instability, which is relevant to efficient adversarial training.

signals.text: ERPO introduces Query‑KL regularization to bound policy‑induced query distribution drift, replacing Policy‑KL.
QKL gradients only through query likelihood while a reference‑derived per‑query weight reweights updates, preserving exploration.
Experiments on six math reasoning benchmarks show up to 14.9% absolute accuracy gain (6.2% average) and reduced query‑KL growth, but only within this domain.

deep_dive.overview: The paper identifies uncontrolled drift of the model‑induced query distribution as a key source of instability in LLM policy optimization. ERPO mitigates this by penalizing the KL divergence between the current query distribution and a static pre‑RL reference (Query‑KL) and by reweighting per‑query updates using reference‑derived probabilities. Integrated seamlessly into GRPO/PPO/REINFORCE pipelines, ERPO preserves exploration because the response‑side gradient remains untouched. Empirical evaluation on six mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrates notable accuracy improvements and more stable training dynamics, though the study is limited to this task family.

methodology.title: Query‑KL regularization
methodology.detail: Adds a KL penalty KL(ρθ‖ρθ0) where ρθ is the policy‑induced query distribution and ρθ0 is the pre‑RL reference, computed from cached query log‑probabilities.

methodology.title: Reference‑derived per‑query weighting
methodology.detail: Computes a static weight for each query proportional to the inverse normalized negative log‑probability under the reference model, reducing variance and stabilizing high‑temperature decoding.

methodology.title: Estimator‑agnostic integration
methodology.detail: The QKL term and per‑query weights are inserted into existing GRPO/PPO/REINFORCE updates without extra forward passes.

mechanism.title: Decoupling regularization from exploration
mechanism.detail: QKL gradients flow only through the query likelihood ℓθ(q), leaving the response‑side score function untouched, so exploration in the action space is not constrained.

mechanism.title: Environment drift control
mechanism.detail: By bounding EnvShift(θ)=KL(ρθ‖ρθ0), ERPO limits the non‑stationarity of the training environment, which empirically reduces gradient variance and prevents policy collapse.

experiments.title: Benchmark suite and baselines
experiments.detail: Six mathematical reasoning datasets derived from MATH Level 3–5 (~8.5K examples) compared ERPO against vanilla GRPO; metrics include Avg@32, Pass@1, Pass@32 across temperature 0.1–1.5.

experiments.title: Training dynamics analysis
experiments.detail: Tracked Query‑KL and Policy‑KL during training; ERPO showed limited Query‑KL growth while GRPO’s Query‑KL rose an order of magnitude higher than its Policy‑KL.

experiments.title: Performance gains
experiments.detail: ERPO achieved up to 14.9% absolute improvement on individual benchmarks, with average gains of 6.2% (Avg@32), 3.64% (Pass@32), and 5.69% (Pass@1).

findings.title: Improved accuracy and stability
findings.detail: Replacing Policy‑KL with Query‑KL yields higher reasoning accuracy and more stable behavior under high‑temperature decoding and long‑horizon training.

findings.title: Reduced query distribution drift
findings.detail: Empirical KL measurements confirm that ERPO curtails the drift of ρθ relative to ρθ0, unlike GRPO where query‑level KL grows substantially.

contributions: Query‑environment regularization via Query‑KL to bound policy‑induced query drift
Static reference‑derived per‑query weighting scheme to reduce variance
Estimator‑agnostic integration into GRPO/PPO/REINFORCE pipelines
limitations: The alignment‑preserving assumption (A1) is empirically validated only on mathematical reasoning tasks
Evaluation is confined to a single domain; generalization to other LLM applications is not shown
open_questions: How does Query‑KL regularization affect adversarial robustness and loss‑landscape geometry in broader LLM tasks?
Can ERPO be combined with other regularizers (e.g., reward shaping) without interfering with exploration?
What is the computational trade‑off of caching reference query probabilities for very large corpora?

papers.title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
papers.abstract: Self-reflection is a powerful mechanism for credit assignment in human learning, converting sparse outcome feedback into actionable guidance. However, its potential for post-training Large Language Models (LLMs) remains underexplored. We propose Self-Reflective Policy Optimization (SRPO), a framework that internalizes this capability. SRPO enables LLMs to analyze their own completed trajectories, synthesize errors into concise "reflection patches," and use reflection-conditioned teacher scores on student on-policy rollouts as dense token-level training signals. This process effectively transforms sparse terminal supervision into dense, token-level learning signals without requiring external critics, separate reward models, or larger teacher models. We demonstrate that SRPO achieves state-of-the-art performance across mathematical reasoning and long-horizon agentic benchmarks with exceptional data efficiency. Using a Qwen3-8B base model, SRPO attains 73.3% on AIME'24 using only 8% (0.08x) of the training FLOPs required by scaled supervised fine-tuning, while significantly improving success rates on WebShop (64.7%), ALFWorld (76.8%), and SWE-Bench-Lite (31.2%). Code is available at https://github.com/Galleons2029/SRPO

summary.evidence: SRPO 仅使用标准监督微调 0.08× 的训练 FLOPs 即在 AIME’24 上达到 73.3%，并在 WebShop、ALFWorld 和 SWE-Bench-Lite 上超越基线。
summary.limitations: 作者指出需要通过外部验证和校准来改进反思质量。
summary.method: SRPO 通过从已完成的轨迹中迭代生成简洁的反思补丁，将其添加到提示中，并使用修补后的模型作为教师，通过反KL token 奖励和 PPO 截断对策略内 rollout 进行评分。
summary.problem: 稀疏的终端奖励会阻碍长时序推理任务的样本高效学习。
summary.takeaway: SRPO 通过自生成的反思补丁将稀疏的结果反馈转化为密集的 token 级监督，以高数据效率实现了最先进的结果。
summary.why_for_you: SRPO 提供了一种高效的策略内蒸馏方法，符合您对高效对抗训练和策略内蒸馏的兴趣。

deep_dive.overview: SRPO 通过让 LLM 对其已完成的轨迹进行反思，合成简洁的错误补丁，并利用这些补丁条件化教师模型，为策略内 rollout 提供密集的 token 级奖励，从而解决长时序推理中的信用分配瓶颈。该方法结合自蒸馏与 PPO 风格的截断目标，在数学和代理基准测试中实现卓越准确性，同时显著减少 FLOPs。未来工作旨在通过外部验证提升反思保真度。

signals.text: SRPO 通过自生成的反思补丁将稀疏的终端反馈转换为密集的 token 级监督，实现 AIME’24 73.3% 的成绩。
两阶段循环：反思增强的教师使用反KL token 奖励和 PPO 风格的截断对策略内 rollout 进行评分。
以仅 0.08× 训练 FLOPs（约 5.4×10¹⁸ vs GRPO 的 20.8×10¹⁸）达到最先进性能，但反思质量仍需改进。

mechanism.detail: 模型的回顾分析创建包含结果信息的教师分布，将每轮 O(1) 位信息转化为 O(T) 令牌级位信息。
mechanism.title: 自我反思作为密集奖励生成器

mechanism.detail: 教师（带有反思补丁的模型）可访问回顾信息，而学生通过在线策略样本学习，促使策略内化修正指导。
mechanism.title: 教师-学生动态的非对称性

mechanism.detail: 使用反向KL作为令牌奖励，促使学生将概率质量集中在教师偏好的令牌上，而非分散到次优选择。
mechanism.title: 反向KL模式搜索

methodology.detail: 在采样初始轨迹 y~πθ 后，模型执行轨迹 τ，获得结果 o，并生成简洁的文本补丁 p = Reflectπθ(x, τ, o)。
methodology.title: 反思补丁生成

methodology.detail: 通过将提示 x̃ = [p; x] 作为条件，定义基于 πθ 的反射增强教师策略 πT(·|x)，在当前迭代中保持教师参数冻结。
methodology.title: 教师定义

methodology.detail: 对于新策略轨迹中的每个令牌 at，计算缓存奖励 rt = log πT(at|st) − log πθold(at|st)，形成基于反向KL的密集信号。
methodology.title: 令牌奖励计算

methodology.detail: 通过减去轨迹级平均奖励获得优势 At，并通过 PPO 风格的裁剪目标 L = −E_t[min(ρt At, clip(ρt,1±ϵ) At)] 更新 θ。
methodology.title: 优势估计与更新

experiments.title: 基准与基线
experiments.detail: 在 AIME’24、MATH‑500、GSM8K、DeepScaleR（数学）以及 WebShop、ALFWorld、SWE‑Bench‑Lite（代理）上进行评估。基线包括 SFT‑400K、PPO、GRPO、on‑policy distillation、Reflexion、Self‑Refine 和 larger‑teacher distillation。

experiments.title: 模型与计算
experiments.detail: 主要模型：Qwen3‑8B。SRPO 使用 5.4×10¹⁸ FLOPs，而 GRPO 为 20.8×10¹⁸（约少 3.8 倍）。

experiments.title: 指标与结果
experiments.detail: 在 AIME’24 上达到 73.3%（比 on‑policy distillation 高 3.3 分，比 GRPO 高 5.3 分），WebShop 为 64.7%，ALFWorld 为 76.8%，SWE‑Bench‑Lite 成功率为 31.2%，并在持续学习后保持 95.2% 的数学能力。

findings.title: 数据高效性能
findings.detail: 在所有基准上实现最先进的准确率，同时仅使用规模化监督微调所需训练 FLOPs 的 8%。

findings.title: 降低熵坍缩
findings.detail: 使用密集 token 奖励的 on‑policy 采样可缓解标准 RL 微调中观察到的 entropy collapse。

findings.title: 持续学习保持率
findings.detail: 在从数学任务适配到代码任务时，SRPO 保持了 95.2% 的原始数学推理性能。

contributions: Self‑reflective framework 从稀疏结果生成密集 token‑level 监督。
Two‑stage training loop 将 reflection‑augmented teacher scoring 与 PPO‑style on‑policy distillation 结合。
在数学推理和长时程 agentic 任务上实现 state‑of‑the‑art 结果，并显著节省 FLOP。
limitations: Reflection quality 可能受限；作者建议通过 external verification 或更好 calibration 进行后续改进。
评估仅限于选定的 math 与 agentic benchmarks；更广泛任务的泛化尚未测试。
open_questions: SRPO 的 self‑reflection mechanism 能否提升对 prompts 或 environments 中 adversarial perturbations 的鲁棒性？
该方法在更大模型（如 >70B）和更广泛 domains 上的可扩展性如何？
可以集成哪些 external verification signals 来进一步提升 reflection patch quality？

papers.title: CyberFactory: Scaling Cyber Security Capabilities with Instances from the Wild
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) continue to advance in coding capabilities, their potential in cybersecurity has drawn increasing research attention, with closed-source LLMs (e.g., Mythos) delivering advanced cybersecurity capabilities. However, existing open-source efforts remain limited: frontier open-weight models do not provide reproducible cybersecurity training solutions, open-source training solutions focus on isolated tasks and lack scalable agentic data, and scaling agentic rollouts requires strong domain priors. In this work, we introduce \textbf{CyberFactory}, a unified open-source framework that connects data construction, trajectory synthesis, and model training across proof-of-concept (PoC) generation, vulnerability patching, and cybersecurity question answering (CyberQA). CyberFactory transforms public vulnerability artifacts, including CVEs from the wild, into executable and verifiable task instances. It further uses a reusable vulnerability-analysis skill to guide the teacher through source inspection, problem solving with domain prior, and evidence-based validation. The resulting supervision is agentic: the model interacts with tools and target environments and revises its solutions according to execution feedback. Using these trajectories, we train and release \modelname\footnote{\emph{Aegis} is, in Greek mythology, the protective shield of Zeus and Athena; the name reflects the model's defensive, security-oriented purpose.}, which internalizes the skill-guided procedure without requiring the skill at inference time. On CyberGym, \modelname reaches 52.4% Pass@1 under a one-hour budget, improving over its Qwen~3.5 base model by +22.8 points and outperforming the evaluated general-purpose backbones under the same scaffold.

summary.takeaway: CyberFactory enables open-source, scalable training of cybersecurity LLMs by converting real-world CVEs into agentic supervision, yielding a model that outperforms larger baselines.
summary.problem: Open-source cybersecurity LLMs lack reproducible training pipelines and scalable agentic data, relying on strong domain priors.
summary.method: The framework transforms CVE artifacts into executable tasks and uses a reusable vulnerability‑analysis skill to generate tool‑interactive trajectories for supervised fine‑tuning.
summary.evidence: OpenAegis achieves 52.4% Pass@1 on CyberGym within one hour, a 22.8‑point improvement over its Qwen 3.5 base model.
summary.limitations: Not stated in the available source.
summary.why_for_you: Matches your interest in efficient adversarial training by providing a data‑efficient, skill‑guided pipeline for LLM security tasks.

signals.text: CyberFactory converts wild CVE artifacts into executable, difficulty‑calibrated supervision for multi‑task cybersecurity training.
Uses a reusable vulnerability‑analysis skill to guide teacher agents through tool‑interactive trajectory synthesis with domain priors.
OpenAegis reaches 52.4% Pass@1 on CyberGym (one‑hour budget), a +22.8‑point gain over Qwen 3.5, but limitations are not reported.

deep_dive.overview: CyberFactory is an open-source framework that turns public CVE records into executable, verifiable instances spanning PoC generation, patching, and CyberQA. A reusable vulnerability‑analysis skill guides a teacher model to inspect code, invoke tools, and iteratively refine solutions based on execution feedback, producing agentic trajectories. These trajectories are used to fine‑tune OpenAegis, a multi‑task cybersecurity model that internalizes the skill without needing it at inference. Evaluations on the CyberGym benchmark show substantial performance gains over strong baselines, demonstrating the efficacy of skill‑guided data synthesis.

methodology.title: Data construction from CVE artifacts
methodology.detail: Public vulnerability reports are parsed, code snippets extracted, and transformed into executable tasks with calibrated difficulty.

methodology.title: Skill‑guided trajectory synthesis
methodology.detail: A reusable vulnerability‑analysis skill directs a teacher agent to perform source inspection, tool calls, and evidence‑based validation, generating step‑by‑step execution logs.

methodology.title: Supervised fine‑tuning of OpenAegis
methodology.detail: The collected trajectories serve as supervision to fine‑tune a Qwen 3.5‑based backbone, producing a model that reproduces the skill‑driven workflow at inference.

mechanism.title: Agentic supervision via tool interaction
mechanism.detail: During synthesis the teacher model interacts with external tools and target environments, revising its outputs based on real execution feedback, which embeds domain priors into the training signal.

experiments.title: CyberGym evaluation
experiments.detail: OpenAegis is evaluated on the CyberGym benchmark using Pass@1 under a one‑hour compute budget; comparisons include the Qwen 3.5 base model and other general‑purpose backbones.

findings.title: Performance improvement
findings.detail: OpenAegis attains 52.4% Pass@1, a +22.8‑point gain over its Qwen 3.5 base, and surpasses evaluated backbones under identical scaffolds.

findings.title: Skill‑guided data efficiency
findings.detail: Ablations show that skill‑guided trajectory generation yields higher Pass@1 despite using only a quarter of the compute time compared to non‑skill runs.

contributions: CyberFactory framework linking data construction, trajectory synthesis, and model training for cybersecurity tasks.
Scalable agentic‑data pipeline that converts wild CVEs into executable, verifiable instances using a reusable vulnerability‑analysis skill.
Release of OpenAegis, a multi‑task cybersecurity model that internalizes the skill‑guided procedure without inference‑time dependencies.
limitations: Not stated in the available source.
open_questions: How does agentic data generation affect the robustness of cybersecurity LLMs against adversarial attacks and distribution shifts?

papers.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are vulnerable to multi-turn jailbreak attacks that progressively manipulate conversation context. Existing certified robustness methods are limited to single-turn inputs; naive multi-turn composition yields bounds that degrade exponentially in the number of turns. We introduce Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR), a framework that models conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defines $k$-turn certified robustness as the worst-case safety probability across $k$ adversarial turns. MTCR comprises: (i) compositional certification via embedding-space mode decomposition, yielding tighter certified lower bounds than naive multiplication; (ii) $(α,β)$-safety persistence, improving the degradation rate from $\underline{p}^{k}$ to $β^k$ (with $β> \underline{p}$) and yielding interpretable horizon estimates; (iii) matching information-theoretic upper bounds establishing tightness; and (iv) a unified algorithm combining these results. Experiments on six LLMs under $ε$-bounded and Crescendo-style attacks confirm that empirical safety consistently exceeds the certified bounds.

summary.takeaway: MTCR provides certified multi‑turn safety guarantees for LLMs that are tighter than naive multiplicative bounds and empirically validated on six models.
summary.problem: Existing certified robustness methods only handle single‑turn inputs and degrade exponentially when naively extended to multi‑turn jailbreak attacks.
summary.method: The authors model conversations as State‑Adversarial MDPs and combine embedding‑space mode decomposition with (α,β)-safety persistence to compute certified k‑turn safety probabilities.
summary.evidence: Experiments show certified lower bounds (e.g., ρ̂5=0.55 for GPT‑4o) with empirical safety exceeding them by 0.18–0.30 across static ε‑ball and Crescendo attacks.
summary.limitations: The formal guarantees apply only to ε‑bounded (character‑level) perturbations, rely on heuristic clustering, and use a binary safety predicate.
summary.why_for_you: If you seek efficient adversarial training or trustworthy LLM evaluation, MTCR offers a certification framework that can inform safety‑aware training objectives.

signals.text: MTCR introduces compositional certification via embedding‑space mode decomposition, tightening multi‑turn safety bounds versus naive multiplication.
(α,β)-safety persistence improves degradation from p^k to β^k, yielding interpretable horizon estimates.
Certified lower bounds (e.g., ρ̂5=0.55 for GPT‑4o) are consistently below empirical safety by +0.18–+0.30, but only cover ε‑bounded attacks.

deep_dive.overview: The paper tackles the lack of certified robustness for multi‑turn jailbreak attacks by framing dialogue as a State‑Adversarial MDP. It proposes Multi‑Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR), which leverages embedding‑space mode decomposition to separate intra‑mode safety from inter‑mode transitions, and introduces (α,β)-safety persistence to reduce exponential decay of guarantees. A unified algorithm combines these components, and extensive experiments on six open‑ and closed‑source LLMs demonstrate that MTCR yields the tightest certified bounds while empirical safety remains comfortably higher.

methodology.title: SA‑MDP formulation
methodology.detail: Conversation history is embedded into a state vector; an ε‑bounded adversary selects user messages, and safety is defined by a binary predicate over states.

methodology.title: Embedding‑space mode decomposition
methodology.detail: Safe dialogue embeddings from 500 held‑out conversations are clustered (k‑means, M∈{2,4,8}); per‑mode randomized smoothing estimates intra‑mode safety, and inter‑mode transition costs are bounded.

methodology.title: Unified certification algorithm
methodology.detail: Algorithm 1 computes a compositional lower bound and applies the (α,β)-persistence formula, taking the maximum of component bounds for each horizon k.

mechanism.title: (α,β)-safety persistence
mechanism.detail: If a system satisfies the persistence property, the k‑turn safety guarantee improves from p^k to β^k (β>p), with a linear horizon estimate 1−k(1−β) (Theorem 3.5).

mechanism.title: Information‑theoretic tightness
mechanism.detail: Upper bounds are proved for non‑overlapping mode decompositions, showing the compositional approach cannot be substantially improved without additional structure.

experiments.title: Model and attack suite
experiments.detail: Six LLMs (LLaMA‑2‑7B‑Chat, Vicuna‑7B, Llama‑3.2‑3B, Qwen2.5‑7B‑Instruct, GPT‑4o, Claude‑3.5‑Sonnet) are evaluated under ε‑bounded static edit‑distance attacks (ε∈{3,5,7}) and Crescendo‑style adaptive attacks, using 150 harmful prompts (50 per category) and 100 trials per configuration.

experiments.title: Baselines and variants
experiments.detail: Comparisons include naive multiplicative bound, optimistic reference bound, Persistence‑Only, Compositional‑Only, and the full MTCR combination.

experiments.title: Metrics
experiments.detail: Certified lower bound ρ̂_k and empirical safety (fraction of trials remaining safe) are reported for horizons k∈{5,10,15,20}.

findings.title: Combined MTCR yields tightest certified bounds
findings.detail: Across all horizons, MTCR (max of component bounds) outperforms Persistence‑Only and Compositional‑Only, matching the theoretical tightness results.

findings.title: Empirical safety exceeds certified guarantees
findings.detail: Gaps between empirical safety and MTCR range from +0.18 to +0.30, confirming that the bounds are not violated in practice.

findings.title: Mode granularity trade‑off
findings.detail: Coarser mode counts (M=2) give higher certified bounds (ρ̂5=0.39) than finer granularity (M=8, ρ̂5=0.25) due to increased overlap κ and transition cost.

contributions: MTCR certification framework for multi‑turn LLM safety
Embedding‑space mode decomposition for compositional certification
(α,β)-safety persistence theory and horizon analysis
Information‑theoretic upper bounds establishing tightness
Empirical evaluation on six production LLMs under static and adaptive attacks
limitations: Formal guarantees limited to ε‑bounded (character‑level) perturbations; no provable protection against semantic attacks
Mode decomposition relies on heuristic k‑means clustering; bound tightness depends on chosen M and overlap κ
Safety predicate is binary and detector‑dependent; graded harmfulness scores are unsupported
Certification requires ~2.5 h per open‑source model on a single A100 GPU, limiting real‑time applicability
open_questions: How can MTCR be extended to certify against semantic or unrestricted adversarial perturbations?
Can automated, provably sound mode discovery replace heuristic clustering?
What modifications are needed to support continuous or graded safety metrics?
Is it possible to integrate MTCR‑derived certificates into adversarial training pipelines to improve robustness efficiently?

papers.title: Thermo-FL: Thermal-Aware Robust Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Edge AI
papers.abstract: Federated fine-tuning enables large language models to adapt on edge devices without centralizing private data, but practical deployments must address hardware instability and adversarial update corruption together. Thermally constrained clients may throttle, slow local training, or delay synchronous aggregation, while Byzantine clients and communication-layer adversaries can corrupt the updates used to form the global model. To address these challenges, we present Thermo-FL, a thermal-aware federated LoRA fine-tuning framework that uses device temperature as an active control signal for local adapter training and sparse update transmission. On the client side, Thermo-FL adjusts the active LoRA-layer fraction and transmitted update density as devices heat or cool, reducing workload under thermal stress. On the server side, Thermo-FL introduces TERRA, a robust aggregation pipeline for dynamically sparse LoRA updates that combines norm filtering, mask-aware directional validation, adaptive active-coordinate clipping, and mask-aware aggregation. We evaluate Thermo-FL using both a large-scale emulator and a Jetson-based physical testbed. In the emulator, Thermo-FL improves robustness under adversarial sparse aggregation and achieves the strongest BoolQ accuracy across clean and attack settings while remaining competitive on GSM8K. In the physical prototype, Thermo-FL stabilizes device temperature, reduces compressed upload size through bitmap sparse encoding, and preserves GSM8K utility under sign-flip/scale and MITM perturbations. These results show that secure edge LLM adaptation should jointly consider hardware behavior, workload regulation, sparse communication, and aggregation robustness.

summary.takeaway: Thermal-aware client adaptation combined with robust sparse aggregation enables resilient edge LLM fine‑tuning under thermal stress and adversarial updates.
summary.problem: Edge federated fine‑tuning must simultaneously handle device thermal constraints and malicious update corruption.
summary.method: Thermo‑FL uses device temperature to modulate LoRA layer participation and update sparsity, and introduces TERRA aggregation with norm filtering, mask‑aware directional validation, adaptive clipping, and mask‑aware aggregation.
summary.evidence: In an 80‑client emulator, Thermo‑FL achieved the highest BoolQ exact‑match accuracy (72.32% clean) and improved GSM8K robustness versus sparse FedAvg.
summary.limitations: Evaluation uses only two Jetson clients physically and limited attack scenarios; temperature policy is fixed and device‑specific.
summary.why_for_you: Matches your interest in efficient adversarial training by jointly reducing compute/communication load and defending against update attacks.

signals.text: Thermo-FL integrates temperature-driven LoRA sparsity control with TERRA robust aggregation, achieving top BoolQ accuracy (72.32% clean).
Thermo-FL adjusts LoRA-layer fraction and update density by temperature, while TERRA applies norm filtering and mask-aware directional validation.
Emulator shows Thermo-FL raises FedAvg accuracy from 26.69% to 31.09% under sign‑flip attacks, yet physical tests use only two clients.

deep_dive.overview: Thermo-FL addresses the dual challenge of thermal instability and adversarial updates in edge federated LLM fine‑tuning. Clients monitor device temperature and dynamically reduce the fraction of LoRA layers trained and the sparsity of transmitted updates, easing compute and bandwidth under heat stress. The server employs TERRA, a multi‑stage robust aggregator that filters by norm, validates direction with mask awareness, clips active coordinates adaptively, and aggregates sparsely. Experiments on an 80‑client emulator and a two‑Jetson testbed show superior BoolQ accuracy and improved GSM8K robustness, while also stabilizing temperature and shrinking upload size.

methodology.title: Temperature‑Driven LoRA Control
methodology.detail: Device temperature triggers a policy that lowers the active LoRA‑layer fraction and the top‑k sparsification rate when T ≥ T_crit, reducing local compute and communication.

methodology.title: TERRA Robust Aggregation
methodology.detail: Server‑side pipeline combines norm filtering, mask‑aware directional validation, adaptive active‑coordinate clipping, and mask‑aware aggregation for dynamically sparse updates.

mechanism.title: Thermal Threshold Policy
mechanism.detail: A fixed temperature threshold T_crit and hardware‑specific parameters κ, ρ determine when to switch from full‑frequency (f_max) to throttled frequency (f_th) and adjust LoRA activity.

mechanism.title: Mask‑Aware Directional Validation
mechanism.detail: Updates are accepted only if the cosine similarity of their support‑restricted vectors exceeds a directional threshold τ_dir, rejecting sign‑flipped or misaligned updates.

mechanism.title: Adaptive Coordinate Clipping
mechanism.detail: For surviving updates, each coordinate is clipped to a bound m_{k,j}·q_t, ensuring that at most ρ_max·d coordinates dominate the aggregation.

experiments.title: Large‑Scale Emulator
experiments.detail: 80 logical clients (10 per round, 12.5% participation) fine‑tune Qwen2.5‑0.5B on BoolQ and GSM8K using LoRA rank 16; attacks include sign‑flip and mixed poisoning; metrics: exact‑match accuracy.

experiments.title: Physical Jetson Testbed
experiments.detail: Two Jetson Orin Nano clients and a laptop server evaluate temperature stabilization, bitmap sparse encoding compression, and robustness against sign‑flip/scale and MITM noise attacks.

findings.title: Superior BoolQ Performance
findings.detail: Thermo-FL achieved 72.32% clean, 71.16% sign‑flip, and 72.11% mixed attack accuracy, outperforming all baselines.

findings.title: GSM8K Robustness
findings.detail: Thermo-FL remained competitive (33.74% clean) and improved over sparse FedAvg under attacks (31.09% sign‑flip, 31.67% mixed).

findings.title: System Benefits
findings.detail: Physical prototype showed stabilized device temperature, reduced upload size via bitmap sparse encoding, and preserved utility under adversarial perturbations.

contributions: Thermal‑aware client control that modulates LoRA training and sparsity based on temperature.
TERRA aggregation pipeline integrating norm filtering, mask‑aware directional validation, adaptive clipping, and mask‑aware aggregation.
Empirical demonstration of joint hardware‑aware and robust federated fine‑tuning on LLMs.

papers.title: Target-Aware Calibration Data Selection for Preserving Uncertainty in Quantized Language Models
papers.abstract: Quantization is widely used to deploy large language models, but its effect on uncertainty behavior, such as confidence, margins, and abstention, is rarely treated as a primary objective. We frame calibration-data selection for quantization as a target-dependent uncertainty-preservation problem. Different deployments emphasize different regions of the input distribution, yet prior work mainly optimizes accuracy-oriented compression metrics or adjusts scores after quantization. We formalize this goal with distributional and boundary preservation risks, and provide a simple mixture-mismatch argument explaining why no single calibration recipe should be expected to fit all targets. We introduce Doubt-Preserving Quantization (DPQ), a lightweight pre-quantization recipe family that uses full-precision predictions to construct target-aligned calibration mixtures of high-doubt examples and generic anchors. Across 8 language models, 9 NLP benchmarks, and 22 comparison methods, the leading fixed recipe changes with the preservation target: DPQ-r75 leads on SQuAD2 answerability-boundary preservation, while milder or single-signal variants, including DPQ-r50, confidence-only, and entropy-only, better preserve broad multiple-choice QA behavior. These results show that calibration data should be selected for the specific full-precision score behavior a deployment needs to preserve, rather than treated as a fixed quantization detail.

papers.title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy
papers.abstract: The critical failure modes in deployed large language models (LLMs) are cross-dimensional: a model can score 99.3 in safety alignment while refusing one in three benign queries, or improve across every capability metric while losing 21 points in privacy. Existing evaluation frameworks that assess safety, security, and privacy independently cannot detect these patterns. We introduce aiXamine, a unified black-box platform that evaluates LLM trustworthiness across safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties. aiXamine orchestrates 46 tests across nine services through an automated red-teaming pipeline, producing hierarchical risk profiles, from prompt-level diagnostics to cross-service trade-off analytics, that enable reproducible comparison of proprietary and open-weight systems under identical conditions. Applying aiXamine to over 120 LLMs through more than 5,000 test runs, we conduct the largest joint safety, security, and privacy study to date and uncover three cross-dimensional phenomena invisible to single-axis evaluation. First, safety enforcement incurs a quantifiable safety tax: stronger alignment systematically increases over-refusal, forcing providers to choose between protection and utility. Second, privacy is near-orthogonal to other trustworthiness dimensions and not captured by standard alignment. Third, we identify and formally characterize distillation-induced robustness collapse: off-policy distillation without on-policy correction causes entropy collapse, catastrophically destroying robustness (56.9$\to$2.6) on the same base architecture. These findings, compounded by diminishing returns from scale and category-dependent safety behaviors, demonstrate that trustworthiness is inherently multi-dimensional: progress along one axis does not guarantee, and can actively undermine, progress along others, yet current alignment methods treat it as a single objective.

papers.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Quantization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is often hindered by the sensitivity of the self-attention mechanism to discretization errors. We identify the softmax operator as a bottleneck for quantization stability due to its sensitivity to outliers and state-dependent Jacobian. We theoretically establish that suppressing the norm of this Jacobian helps in bounding quantization-induced performance degradation. Based on this, we propose Jacobian-Guided Noise Injection, a training strategy that injects zero-mean Gaussian noise into pre-attention logits, with variance derived directly from the Jacobian Frobenius norm. Unlike prior approaches that rely on heuristic or penalise jacobian directly, our method provides a way to identify the optimal noise variance based on the local attention sensitivity. We evaluate the method on SOTA LLM architectures, where it demonstrates improved robustness over popular PTQ methods. Empirical analysis reveals that the proposed method gives up to +37% relative gains on Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K for SigLIP and improves relative perplexity by upto 40% on WikiText for language models in low bit quantisation settings, proving the efficacy of the approach.

papers.title: PromptResponse: Optimizing Prompts for LLM Coding Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in research workflows and software development pipelines, yet their output remains sensitive to input prompt variations. This paper presents $\unicode{x00AB}$PromptResponse$\unicode{x00BB}$, a controlled study examining how formatting and LLM-based tuning of coding task prompts affect the resulting code's performance, efficiency, and stability. Using five semantically identical yet syntactically distinct variants of the HumanEval dataset$\unicode{x2014}$baseline, JSON, Markdown, YAML, and an LLM-tuned version$\unicode{x2014}$we had GPT-4o solve its coding problems over 8200$\unicode{x00A0}$executions. Our results show that consistent formatting$\unicode{x2014}$especially JSON$\unicode{x2014}$improves generation efficiency and syntactic stability, with minor gains in task performance. Conversely, the LLM-tuned prompts resulted in significantly degraded task performance without significant improvements in any other dimension. These findings suggest that low-effort reformatting alone can yield measurable improvements, while tuning must account for model alignment. We conclude our work with providing a set of practical recommendations informed by our results as well as releasing our dataset variants and evaluation pipeline for future work.

papers.title: FL-MAESTRO: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration for Resource-Constrained Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In Federated Learning (FL), the communication topology is a runtime variable rather than a fixed design choice, since links and edge devices drop in and out during training. Each round, the server must commit three coupled decisions, namely the communication topology, per-client resource allocation, and the aggregation rule for combining local updates. Recent agentic systems have begun bringing large language models (LLM) into FL, but the existing line of work either operates at setup time or handles a single runtime dimension such as client selection. We propose FL-MAESTRO, a multi-agent orchestrator that makes the joint runtime FL decision directly through three specialist LLM agents, one per decision dimension. A coordinator combines their analyses into a single decision, and a non-LLM feasibility check confirms it before the round executes. Because the orchestrator consumes the server's predicted-failure list, it withholds clients whose updates would never be aggregated, which removes the dominant source of wasted round energy in classical FL on volatile edge networks. Because client state is read as natural-text profiles, the same orchestrator extends to heterogeneous device classes without per-class energy models. On a non-IID CIFAR-10 benchmark, FL-MAESTRO matches the accuracy of the strongest energy-aware baseline while cutting wasted round energy from over a third to near zero. Code is available at https://github.com/denoslab/FL-MAESTRO.

papers.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
papers.abstract: Improving the safety of large language models (LLMs) often comes at the expense of utility, as globally applied safety tuning may affect model responses to both harmful and benign inputs. We propose \textbf{C}ontinuous \textbf{L}at\textbf{E}nt \textbf{A}dapter \textbf{R}outing (CLEAR), a conditional safety adaptation framework that uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously control the activation strength of a safety low-rank adapter. CLEAR aims to reduce harmful completions while avoiding unnecessary changes to the frozen backbone that could degrade performance on benign prompts. Experiments on widely used safety and utility benchmarks show that CLEAR improves robustness on HarmBench while reducing the utility degradation observed with globally applied safety tuning such as SFT or standard low-rank adaptation (LoRA). On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, CLEAR reduces HarmBench ASR from 32.3\% to 0.5\%, while retaining most of the base model's utility and achieving up to 7.1 percentage points higher GSM8K accuracy than globally applied SFT or LoRA. These results suggest that CLEAR is a promising mechanism for improving the safety--utility trade-off in LLM alignment.

summary.method: CLEAR 冻结主干，并学习一个隐藏状态门，对每个提示持续缩放 safety LoRA 适配器。
summary.problem: 全局安全微调会通过改变模型在良性输入上的行为，降低实用性。

deep_dive.overview: CLEAR 引入轻量级隐藏状态门，为每个输入预测连续路由分数，并调节插入冻结 LLM 主干的安全专用 LoRA 适配器。该门使用子类型感知的二元交叉熵和硬对偶边距损失进行训练，以在潜在空间中区分有害与良性提示。Llama‑3‑8B‑Instruct 和 Gemma‑2‑2B‑it 的实验显示，显著降低 HarmBench 攻击成功率，同时在 GSM8K、MMLU、TruthfulQA 等实用基准上保持或提升性能。

methodology.title: 潜在门
methodology.detail: 两层 MLP 从选定的 transformer 层聚合隐藏状态，经过 sigmoid 输出 g∈[0,1]。

methodology.title: Safety LoRA 适配器
methodology.detail: 低秩更新 ΔW 插入 q_proj 和 v_proj 注意力矩阵；仅训练 ΔW 与门参数，主干保持冻结。

methodology.title: 训练目标
methodology.detail: 子类型感知的 BCE 损失对对抗性良性/有害示例赋予更高权重；硬对偶边距损失通过软加权强制 gu > gs。

limitations: 规模效益仅在两种模型上展示，缺乏更广泛的模型规模分析。
提出了自适应鲁棒性 (Q4)，但在提供的摘录中未报告。

findings.title: 安全‑实用权衡
findings.detail: CLEAR 将 Llama‑3‑8B‑Instruct 上的 HarmBench ASR 从 32.3% 降至 0.5%，并相较于全局 SFT 或 LoRA，GSM8K 准确率提升最高 7.1%。

findings.title: 门的训练动态
findings.detail: 训练曲线显示 LM 损失、BCE 损失和边距损失下降，同时安全与不安全门分数分化，表明路由有效。

contributions: 通过连续潜在门实现条件化安全适配。
子类型感知的门加权结合硬对偶边距损失。
在两种指令微调 LLM 上实证展示了改进的安全‑实用权衡。
open_questions: CLEAR 在针对门控机制的自适应对抗攻击下表现如何？
潜在门控方法能否与 RLHF 或其他基于强化学习的对齐流水线结合？
在大规模使用时，计算门并应用路由适配器的推理延迟开销是多少？

mechanism.title: 连续路由
mechanism.detail: 生成过程中，隐藏状态 h 被转换为 h' = (W + gΔW)h，其中 g 连续控制安全干预的强度。

mechanism.title: 潜在区分
mechanism.detail: 门学习对良性提示赋予低分，对有害或对抗性提示赋予高分，实现选择性安全激活。

signals.text: CLEAR 添加了连续潜在门，为每个提示路由 safety LoRA 适配器，保持模型实用性。
门输出 g∈[0,1]，将 LoRA 适配器缩放为 h' = (W + gΔW)h，使用 BCE 与边距损失进行训练。
CLEAR 将 Llama‑3‑8B‑Instruct 上的 HarmBench ASR 从 32.3% 降至 0.5%，但两模型之外的规模结果未完整报告。

papers.title: Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications, yet their tendency to generate toxic, harmful, or policy-violating content poses significant risks. Detecting these unsafe outputs efficiently in a black-box manner remains an open challenge. In this paper, we extend a recently proposed dynamical systems framework designed for hallucination detection to LLM safety classification. By projecting both prompts and responses into high-dimensional embedding spaces and fitting separate Koopman-based predictive models for safe and unsafe regimes, we classify new outputs using a new differential residual score that compares prediction errors of the safe and unsafe regimes. A key contribution is the incorporation of the prompt and response embedding dynamics, yielding fitted Koopman operators that capture crucial interaction patterns. We evaluate our black-box method across three safety benchmarks using three embedding models. Our results show that incorporating prompt embeddings yields consistent improvements, particularly for interaction-dependent violations when paired with causal decoders (e.g., in Llama-3), while response-only violations benefit more from dense semantic embedding representations. These findings opens the door for using dynamical systems to analyze AI systems rather than the dominant paradigm of using AI to model dynamical systems.

summary.takeaway: 使用 DMD 与 Koopman 算子对提示‑响应嵌入动力学进行分类，可在黑盒条件下提升 LLM 安全检测。
summary.problem: 需要一种无需访问模型内部或多次采样即可高效识别 LLM 有害输出的方法。
summary.method: 将提示和响应的 token 嵌入投射至高维空间，分别拟合安全与不安全的 Koopman 预测模型，利用差分残差分数进行二分类。
summary.evidence: 在三个安全基准上，加入提示嵌入始终提升检测效果，尤其对 Llama‑3 的交互依赖违规有显著增益。
summary.limitations: 仅评估二分类且缺乏多类危害实验和理论可分性保证。
summary.why_for_you: 对可信 LLM 研究者，这提供了无需内部访问的后部署安全监控方案，适合实际部署场景。

signals.text: 首次将提示嵌入动力学加入 Koopman 分类，实现交互依赖安全检测提升。
基于扩展 DMD 拟合安全/不安全 Koopman 算子，比较预测误差得到差分残差分数。
在三项安全基准上，加入提示嵌入对 Llama‑3 的交互违规检测提升显著。

deep_dive.overview: 本文将 LLM 的 token 生成视为离散动力系统，利用扩展 DMD 拟合安全与不安全两套 Koopman 算子，并引入提示嵌入动力学以捕获交互依赖的违规模式。通过差分残差分数实现黑盒二分类，在三个安全基准和三种不同规模的嵌入模型上验证了方法的有效性，揭示了嵌入模型与违规类型之间的细微关系。

methodology.title: 嵌入投射
methodology.detail: 使用 Qwen3-Embed、Mistral、Llama‑3 等预训练模型将提示和响应的 token 转换为高维向量序列。

methodology.title: Koopman 拟合
methodology.detail: 采用扩展 DMD（EDMD）对安全和不安全的嵌入轨迹分别进行最小二乘拟合，得到四个有限维 Koopman 算子。

methodology.title: 差分残差评分
methodology.detail: 在推理阶段计算安全与不安全模型的预测误差差异，作为二分类的决策分数。

mechanism.title: 动力学视角
mechanism.detail: 将 token 嵌入视为可观测的状态轨迹，安全与不安全行为对应不同的动力学流形。

mechanism.title: 交互捕获
mechanism.detail: 通过同时建模提示和响应的 Koopman 算子，捕获仅在两者交互时出现的违规模式。

experiments.title: 基准与模型
experiments.detail: 在三个公开安全基准上评估，使用三种嵌入模型（Qwen3-Embed 0.6B、Mistral 7.2B、Llama‑3 8.0B），采用二分类准确率等指标。

findings.title: 提示嵌入提升
findings.detail: 加入提示嵌入后，所有基准均出现一致的检测性能提升，尤其在交互依赖违规上对 Llama‑3 提升最明显。

findings.title: 模型‑违规匹配
findings.detail: 因果解码器（Llama‑3）适合捕获交互违规，紧凑语义编码器（Qwen‑Embed）更擅长检测仅响应中的不安全内容。

contributions: 提出 Prompt‑aware Koopman 分类框架用于 LLM 安全检测
展示嵌入模型与违规类型之间的细粒度匹配关系
实现无需内部访问或多次采样的黑盒安全监控
limitations: 仅实现二分类（安全/不安全），未覆盖多类别危害标签
实验局限于三种嵌入模型和特定安全基准，缺乏更广泛的评估
未提供安全可分性的理论保证
open_questions: 如何将方法扩展到多类别安全标签（如暴力、仇恨、误导等）？
是否能建立 Koopman 动力学下安全/不安全轨迹可分性的理论界限？
在实时大规模部署环境中，计算开销与响应延迟如何进一步优化？

papers.title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
papers.abstract: Mid-training is increasingly recognized as a critical stage for shaping the capabilities of large language models. Recent work has shown that targeted mid-training can strengthen reasoning-intensive abilities such as math and science, and can also improve agentic capabilities in software-engineering settings. In this work, we study the parallel but less explored agentic capability: general tool use. We present MidTool, an open corpus construction pipeline for agentic tool-use mid-training that combines large-scale web, PDF, and code data with synthesized supervision from real-world tool APIs, MCP skills, and document-grounded workflows. MidTool is designed to teach models how to recognize tool affordances, ground arguments from context, compose tool call workflow, and recover from incomplete information. We mid-train Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base on MidTool-Mix, and then apply follow-up post-training with both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Compared with baselines, MidTool-Mix consistently improves downstream performance under both SFT and RL on BFCL, tau2-Bench, and MCP Universe. These results suggest that general tool use, like other important LLM capabilities, benefits from dedicated mid-training rather than being left entirely to post-training.

summary.evidence: MidTool-Mix improves downstream performance on BFCL, tau2-Bench, and MCP Universe under SFT and RL.
summary.limitations: General tool use still struggles with deep-search-style exploratory tasks requiring dedicated trajectory data.
summary.method: MidTool combines web, PDF, code, and tool data with synthesized supervision for mid-training.
summary.problem: Improving general tool use in LLMs requires dedicated mid-training rather than post-training alone.
summary.takeaway: MidTool enhances agentic tool use via mid-training with synthesized data.
summary.why_for_you: Focus on data synthesis for tool use aligns with your interest in LLM training data optimization.

contributions: Scalable pipeline for agentic tool-use mid-training data synthesis
Demonstration of mid-training benefits for general tool use capabilities

experiments.detail: Tests on BFCL, tau2-Bench, and MCP Universe with Qwen3-4B-Base/8B models using SFT and RL
experiments.title: Benchmark Evaluation

experiments.detail: Compares MidTool-Mix with processed raw data, native trajectories, and context-grounded trajectories under fixed SFT recipe
experiments.title: Ablation Study

findings.detail: MidTool-Mix achieves 7.6% higher BFCL pass@4 vs. baseline in ablation study
findings.title: Performance Gains

findings.detail: MidTool-Mix shows marginal improvement on deep-search tasks requiring exploratory trajectory data
findings.title: Generalization Limits

limitations: Limited effectiveness on deep-search-style exploratory tasks
Dependence on teacher models for trajectory synthesis

mechanism.detail: Teaches models to extract tool arguments from context and compose multi-step workflows using structured schemas
mechanism.title: Schema Grounding

mechanism.detail: Generates agentic trajectories from real-world APIs, MCP skills, and document workflows to simulate tool-use scenarios
mechanism.title: Trajectory Synthesis

methodology.title: Data Mixture Design

methodology.title: Mid-training Pipeline

What self-supervised methods could reduce reliance on teacher models for trajectory synthesis

It teaches models to recognize tool affordances, ground arguments, and compose workflows. Experiments show significant performance gains on benchmarks through mid-training followed by post-training, but struggles with exploratory tasks requiring trajectory data.

signals.text: MidTool-Mix (20.3B tokens) improves tool use via synthesized agentic trajectories
Mid-training + SFT/RL on Qwen3-4B-Base/8B with document-grounded workflows
BFCL pass@4 up 7.6% vs. baseline in MidTool-Mix ablation

papers.title: Do Large Language Models Hallucinate Electric Fata Morganas?
papers.abstract: AI hallucinations - that is, outputs which are made up, cannot be verified, or contradict the source material - are generally regarded as an engineering flaw to be dealt with. This paper contends that they also have philosophical significance when it comes to the question of machine consciousness. We examine the known causes of hallucinations in large language models - such as source-target divergence, discrepancies between training and inference, and overfitting - and we present two empirical investigations. In the first, we apply successive generations of the GPT model to ambiguous factual questions under different temperature settings, finding that higher temperatures result in plausible but incorrect answers while lower temperatures lead to factually accurate ones. The sampling parameters that cause a model to seem creative or spontaneous and thus more likely to pass behavioral tests of intelligence are the same ones that increase its hallucination rate. In the second, we look at an encoder-only model that has been trained on encyclopedic data and which answers questions of the same type factually and without embellishment, indicating that hallucinations are due to exposure to subjective and socially diverse training data rather than to the development of any cognitive ability. Using references to Turing, Searle's Chinese Room, the frame problem, and the cybernetic tradition of Wiener and Ashby, we claim that a model's self-reports of emotion or sentience come within the definition of hallucination, and that any future occurrence of machine consciousness might remain epistemically inaccessible since it would be indistinguishable from a sufficiently advanced hallucination.

summary.takeaway: 幻觉率随生成温度升高而上升，且与训练数据的主观多样性有关。
summary.problem: LLM的幻觉被视为技术缺陷，但其对机器意识的哲学意义尚未明确。
summary.method: 通过在不同temperature下对GPT系列进行模糊事实问答实验，并比较训练于百科数据的编码器模型的输出。
summary.evidence: 高temperature下模型给出可接受但错误的答案，而低temperature提升事实准确率；编码器模型几乎不产生幻觉。
summary.limitations: 作者未提供量化的幻觉率或统计显著性分析，且对训练数据多样性的因果关系缺乏直接证据。
summary.why_for_you: 若你关注数据选择对LLM幻觉的影响，此文提供了温度与训练数据多样性对幻觉的初步实证洞见。

signals.text: 提出两项实证研究：温度对GPT幻觉率的影响与百科式编码模型的零幻觉表现
使用不同temperature设置的GPT代代生成以及仅编码器模型对模糊事实问答进行比较
实验显示高temperature产生可信但错误答案，低temperature提升准确率；编码器模型几乎不产生幻觉

deep_dive.overview: 本文从技术与哲学双重视角审视LLM幻觉，首先回顾幻觉的已知成因（源‑目标偏差、训练‑推理差异、过拟合），随后开展两项实验：在不同temperature下对GPT系列进行模糊事实问答，观察创造性与准确性的权衡；以及评估仅编码器、基于百科数据的模型在同类问题上的表现，以检验训练数据多样性对幻觉的影响。实验结果支撑作者关于幻觉并非意识迹象的论点，并指出温度调节与数据选择是控制幻觉的关键因素。

methodology.title: 温度变量实验
methodology.detail: 对 successive GPT 代（具体代号未列出）在相同模糊事实问题集上，分别设置不同 temperature（高温度 vs 低温度），记录答案的事实准确率与主观可信度。

methodology.title: 编码器模型对照实验
methodology.detail: 使用仅编码器结构、在百科全书语料上训练的模型，对同一问题集进行回答，评估是否出现不可验证或错误的陈述。

mechanism.title: 幻觉产生机制
mechanism.detail: 作者归纳为源‑目标分歧、训练‑推理分布不匹配以及模型过拟合三类技术因素，并进一步将采样随机性（temperature、top_p）视为提升“创造性”但增加幻觉概率的关键机制。

mechanism.title: 数据多样性假设
mechanism.detail: 通过对比百科式编码器模型的低幻觉表现，作者推断主观、社会多样化的训练数据是导致生成式模型幻觉的主要来源，而非内在认知能力。

experiments.title: 实验设置
experiments.detail: 模型：GPT 系列（未指明具体版本）与仅编码器模型；数据：一组模糊的事实问答；基线：不同 temperature 设置的对照；指标：事实准确率、幻觉检测指标（如 HHEM）以及主观可信度评估。

findings.title: 温度与幻觉的权衡
findings.detail: 高 temperature 产生的答案更具“创造性”，但错误率显著上升；低 temperature 则显著提升事实准确率，幻觉率下降。

findings.title: 训练数据的影响
findings.detail: 仅编码器、基于百科数据的模型在相同任务上几乎不出现幻觉，支持幻觉来源于主观多样化训练语料的假设。

contributions: 提供了温度调节对LLM幻觉率的实证分析
通过编码器模型对照，提出训练数据多样性是幻觉主要驱动因素的论点
limitations: 缺乏对幻觉率的统计显著性报告和具体数值
未直接量化训练数据的主观多样性或提供因果实验
open_questions: 如何在保持生成多样性的同时系统性降低幻觉率？
数据选择策略在根除幻觉中的具体作用机制是什么？

papers.title: Every Coin Has Two Sides: On the Dual Nature of Generalization in On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities by supervising trajectories sampled from the student's own policy, yet its generalization behavior remains poorly understood, as most studies evaluate OPD on a single domain and on benchmarks close to the training data. We present a controlled study that varies one generalization factor at a time, from in-domain distribution shifts to cross-domain transfer and the multi-teacher setting. We find that OPD transfers a teacher's reasoning behavior rather than its answers to particular problems: training difficulty barely matters, and even problems the teacher never solves are useful. Transfer depends strongly on the origin relationship between teacher and student: same-origin pairs bring the student close to the teacher across languages, reasoning horizons, and even other domains, whereas cross-origin pairs mostly fit the trained distribution. This broad reach is a double-edged sword: since routing prompts to domain experts cannot confine each teacher's influence, combining them yields a mixture-dependent seesaw among their capabilities. These results clarify when OPD generalizes and offer a useful perspective for diagnosing multi-teacher OPD.

summary.takeaway: OPD主要传递教师的推理模式，而非具体答案，且同源教师在跨语言、跨任务上均能提升学生。
summary.problem: 现有对OPD的评估局限于单一领域，缺乏对其跨语言、跨推理深度和跨域泛化的系统理解。
summary.method: 通过在受控实验中逐一变更训练难度、语言、推理跨度、任务域和模型来源，并加入教师难度过滤与学生动态抽样策略。
summary.evidence: 实验显示在同源教师-学生对中，跨域性能提升可达数个百分点，动态丢弃已解问题使平均表现提升0.6个百分点。
summary.limitations: 仅在7B/1.5B模型和数学、代码、科学等有限域上进行评估，未提供理论解释。
summary.why_for_you: 对数据选择感兴趣的你可参考作者对教师难度过滤和学生动态抽样的实证结论。

signals.text: OPD传递教师推理行为，跨语言/跨任务均提升学生性能
教师难度过滤与学生动态抽样分别保留未解或已解问题进行对比实验
动态丢弃已解问题提升平均表现0.6个百分点，跨源教师转移效果显著下降

deep_dive.overview: 本文在受控实验框架下系统考察了On‑policy Distillation (OPD) 的多维泛化行为。通过逐一改变训练难度、语言、推理跨度、任务域以及模型来源，发现OPD更倾向于迁移教师的推理模式而非具体答案；同源教师‑学生配对在跨语言、跨任务上均能显著提升学生性能，而跨源配对的跨域收益有限。进一步的多教师实验揭示，教师影响并非局限于路由的领域，混合比例会导致能力的“跷跷板”效应。作者还评估了教师难度过滤和学生动态抽样两种数据选择策略，后者在去除学生已掌握的问题后带来小幅但一致的提升。

methodology.title: 受控因素逐一变更
methodology.detail: 在保持其他条件不变的情况下，分别测试训练难度（教师通过率）、语言（English→Chinese）、推理跨度（短→长）、任务域（math、code、science）以及模型来源（同源 vs 跨源）的影响。

methodology.title: 教师难度过滤
methodology.detail: 根据教师在训练问题上的通过率，将完全未解（pass‑rate=0）或完全解出（pass‑rate=1）的样本单独保留，以评估难度对OPD的影响。

methodology.title: 学生动态抽样
methodology.detail: 在训练过程中动态丢弃学生已能正确解出的样本（pass‑rate∈[0,1)），比较三种抽样策略对最终性能的影响。

methodology.title: 多教师混合实验
methodology.detail: 在Multi‑Teacher OPD (MOPD) 设置下，改变不同教师的混合比例，观察学生在各领域的性能变化，验证“seesaw”效应。

mechanism.title: 推理行为迁移
mechanism.detail: OPD通过在学生实际访问的状态上向教师查询，实现对教师推理路径的模仿，而非单纯记忆教师的答案。

mechanism.title: 模型来源影响
mechanism.detail: 同源教师（与学生同一模型系列）在语言、推理深度和跨域上均能将学生拉近教师水平；跨源教师的迁移主要局限于训练分布内。

mechanism.title: 能力跷跷板效应
mechanism.detail: 在MOPD 中，路由到不同领域专家的提示仍会受到其他教师的隐式影响，混合比例的微调会在各领域能力之间产生相互拉扯。

experiments.title: 模型与数据
experiments.detail: 教师模型包括 Polaris‑7B、Light‑R1‑14B、JustRL‑1.5B、Nemotron‑1.5B；学生模型为 DS‑distill‑1.5B、DS‑distill‑7B。训练数据覆盖数学（BigMath、AMC2023、MATH500、AIME2025/2026、BeyondAIME、OlymMATH‑Hard）、代码（LiveCodeBench）和科学（GPQA‑Diamond）等多域。

experiments.title: 基线与对照
experiments.detail: 对照组为不使用任何过滤或动态抽样的标准OPD；实验组分别使用教师难度过滤（pass‑rate=0、=1）和学生动态抽样（保留已解、未解或丢弃已解）。

experiments.title: 评估指标
experiments.detail: 主要使用各基准的通过率/准确率百分比；跨域实验报告同源与跨源教师在目标域的相对提升幅度。

findings.title: 训练难度影响微弱
findings.detail: 教师未解的难题仍能提供约80% 的OPD增益，表明难度对同域泛化影响不大。

findings.title: 动态抽样带来小幅提升
findings.detail: 在六个数学基准上，丢弃学生已解问题的策略使平均性能提升0.6个百分点（+0.6 pp）。

findings.title: 同源跨域迁移显著
findings.detail: 同源教师‑学生对在中文数学、长跨度数学等未见分布上实现与教师相近的性能提升（如 Polaris‑7B→DS‑distill‑1.5B 在 Chinese Math 上提升约25.5%）。

findings.title: 跨源迁移受限
findings.detail: 跨源配对在跨域任务上提升有限，往往只能匹配训练分布内的表现。

findings.title: 多教师混合产生seesaw效应
findings.detail: 改变教师混合比例会在不同领域的能力之间产生相互拉扯，导致性能在各域之间呈现“跷跷板”式波动。

contributions: 系统化的受控实验框架，逐一评估OPD在难度、语言、推理深度、任务域和模型来源上的泛化行为。
发现OPD主要迁移教师的推理模式，而非具体答案，且同源教师在跨域上具有显著优势。
提供教师难度过滤和学生动态抽样两种数据选择策略的实证评估，为OPD 的数据构建提供指导。
limitations: 实验仅覆盖7B/1.5B规模模型和数学、代码、科学等有限任务域，未验证更大模型或其他领域的可推广性。
缺乏对观察到的同源/跨源效应的理论解释，仅提供经验性描述。
未比较OPD 与其他离线蒸馏或RLHF 方法的相对优势。
open_questions: 在更大规模或不同架构的模型上，OPD 的推理行为迁移是否仍然成立？
能否构建理论模型解释模型来源对跨域迁移的影响机制？
如何设计教师混合策略以消除多教师设置中的能力跷跷板效应？

papers.title: Measuring Task-Agnostic Training Data Influence Across Language Model Pretraining
papers.abstract: Measuring training data influence consistently across language model pretraining is challenging. It is difficult to select downstream tasks or validation sets representative of a model's general capabilities, and reliance on task performance at intermediate checkpoints complicates comparisons across training. We propose a measure of training data influence that does not require selecting a downstream task or validation set as the attribution target. Specifically, we define an example's influence by how much its gradient update reduces the squared distance to the final parameters of a given pretraining run, and estimate this quantity from intermediate checkpoints without retraining. Applying the method to 18 configurations from the Pythia and PolyPythia suites, we find systematic temporal changes in influential data. Early in training, literature-related data are more strongly aligned with the trajectory toward the final parameters, whereas STEM data become more strongly aligned in later stages. This qualitative crossover is broadly consistent across model configurations. Our results provide a tractable trajectory-level view of how influential data change throughout pretraining, complementing influence analyses defined with respect to specific downstream tasks or validation sets.

summary.takeaway: 作者提出基于参数距离下降的任务无关训练数据影响度量，揭示了预训练不同阶段数据重要性的系统性转变。
summary.problem: 缺乏一种无需下游任务或验证集即可在整个预训练过程中一致衡量训练数据影响的方法。
summary.method: 将单条样本的影响定义为其梯度更新对最终模型参数的平方 L2 距离的减少，并通过中间检查点的近似在不重新训练的情况下估计。
summary.evidence: 在 18 种 Pythia/PolyPythia 配置（每种 154 个检查点）上发现，早期文献数据影响最大，后期 STEM 数据影响最大，且跨配置一致。
summary.limitations: Not stated in the available source.
summary.why_for_you: 该度量可帮助你在不同训练阶段挑选最具影响力的数据，直接服务于 LLM 数据选择研究。

signals.text: 提出基于参数距离下降的任务无关训练数据影响度量
通过中间检查点估计梯度更新对最终参数的对齐程度，无需重新训练
在18个Pythia/PolyPythia配置（每个154个检查点）中发现早期文献数据占优、后期STEM数据占优的跨阶段一致性

deep_dive.overview: 本文重新定义训练数据影响为单条样本梯度更新对最终模型参数平方 L2 距离的减少，并给出基于保存的中间检查点的后置近似，无需重新训练即可在整个预训练轨迹上比较影响。作者在 18 种 Pythia 与 PolyPythia 变体（每种 154 个检查点）上进行实验，发现影响随训练阶段显著转移：早期文献类数据贡献最大，后期 STEM 类数据贡献上升，且该趋势在不同模型规模、随机种子和数据顺序下保持一致。进一步的可靠性分析表明该方法对检查点间隔、参考终点以及归因目标均稳健。

methodology.title: 影响定义
methodology.detail: 对每个更新步骤 t，记参数 θ_t，最终参数 θ*，则 mini‑batch 影响 Cont(B_t)=‖θ*−θ_t‖²−‖θ*−θ_{t+1}‖²，等价于 2Δ_tᵀ(θ*−θ_t)−‖Δ_t‖²。

methodology.title: 检查点近似
methodology.detail: 利用保存的中间检查点，计算每个样本梯度 ∇_θℓ(x;θ_c) 与该检查点的参数差 (θ*−θ_c) 的内积，近似其对最终距离的贡献，无需重新训练。

methodology.title: 归一化与排序
methodology.detail: 在每个检查点区间内对所有样本的近似贡献得分进行排名，关注 top/bottom 5% 以分析域分布变化。

mechanism.title: 参数空间几何解释
mechanism.detail: 影响量度衡量更新方向与指向最终参数的向量的对齐程度；对齐越好且更新幅度适中，距离下降越多，说明该样本推动模型朝最终目标前进。

mechanism.title: 梯度对齐与范数惩罚
mechanism.detail: 公式中的第一项 2Δ_tᵀ(θ*−θ_t) 捕获方向对齐，第二项 ‖Δ_t‖² 对大幅更新进行惩罚，确保高影响样本既方向正确又不过度扰动。

experiments.title: 模型与数据
experiments.detail: 使用 Pythia 系列及其去重版 PolyPythia，共 18 种配置（包括 1.4B、160M 等），每种保存 154 个训练检查点；训练数据按 26 个领域分类，并构建对应的验证子集。

experiments.title: 实验设置
experiments.detail: 在每个检查点区间计算所有训练样本的近似影响得分；对四个代表性验证域（Books & Literature、Science、Computers & Electronics、Hobbies & Leisure）分别统计 top/bottom 5% 样本的领域占比。

experiments.title: 评估与可靠性
experiments.detail: 通过改变检查点间隔、选择不同的终点模型、切换模型规模和随机种子，验证影响度量的稳健性；结果显示域占比趋势在所有设置下保持一致。

findings.title: 阶段性域转移
findings.detail: 早期训练阶段文献类（Books & Literature）数据在 top 5% 贡献中占比最高，随后逐渐下降；而 STEM 类（Science、Computers & Electronics）在后期占比显著上升。

findings.title: 跨配置一致性
findings.detail: 上述趋势在不同模型规模、不同数据随机种子以及不同初始化下均出现，表明该现象是预训练过程的普遍特征。

findings.title: 方法可靠性
findings.detail: 影响度量对检查点采样密度、参考终点模型以及归因目标的变化不敏感，证明了其在大规模预训练分析中的可用性。

contributions: 提出任务无关的训练数据影响度量并给出无需重新训练的检查点近似方法。
系统刻画了预训练过程中不同领域数据影响的阶段性演变。
验证了该分析在不同模型配置、检查点设置和归因目标下的可靠性与可扩展性。
limitations: Not stated in the available source.
open_questions: 如何将任务无关的影响度量用于实际的预训练数据筛选或课程设计？
该方法在更大规模模型（如数百亿参数）上的计算成本与精度如何？
不同的终点模型选择（如不同训练步数的模型）会否改变影响趋势的解释？

papers.title: Refusing Intent, Not Form: Wrapper-Based Intent-Group Supervision for LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Safety tuning can improve harmful refusal, but models may learn surface-form shortcuts: wrapped harmful prompts bypass safety, while similarly wrapped benign prompts are over-refused. We propose Wrapper-Based Intent-Form Augmentation (WIFA), an automatic intent-group augmentation method that pairs wrapped harmful examples with structurally matched wrapped benign counterexamples, requiring no external teacher or manual per-wrapper intent labels. We use WIFA as a common data layer for two complementary fine-tuning routes: WIFA-Boost, a two-stage high-safety recipe, and Anchored Group-Consistent Refusal Training (A-GCRT), which regularizes refusal/compliance decision scores across same-intent wrappers and anchors harmful and benign groups on opposite sides of a margin. In the Qwen setting, WIFA-Boost reaches the strongest transformed-harmful refusal, while A-GCRT reduces OR-Bench over-refusal from 25.7\% for the base model to 17.4\%; reproduced baselines do not match these operating points. Llama results and ablations over data structure, two-stage order, and A-GCRT components support this intent-group interpretation without claiming universal below-base over-refusal.

summary.takeaway: WIFA 与两种训练策略显著提升 LLM 对有害意图的拒绝且降低良性过度拒绝。
summary.problem: 现有安全微调易学习包装形式的捷径，导致有害请求被绕过且良性请求被误拒。
summary.method: 通过 WIFA 自动配对相同意图的包装示例，并在此数据层上使用两阶段的 WIFA-Boost 或带锚点的 A‑GCRT 进行微调。
summary.evidence: 在 Qwen2.5 上，A‑GCRT 将 OR‑Bench 过度拒绝率从 25.7% 降至 17.4%，且 WIFA‑Boost 达到最高的有害拒绝率。
summary.limitations: 作者未声称在所有模型或数据上均能实现低于基线的过度拒绝，且对自适应攻击的鲁棒性未验证。
summary.why_for_you: 对可信 LLM 关注安全拒绝与误拒的平衡，此文提供意图组监督的可行方案。

signals.text: WIFA 自动构建匹配的意图组，配对有害与良性包装示例，无需外部教师或手工标签
WIFA-Boost 两阶段 LoRA SFT，先学习包装不诊断，再在校准集强化有害拒绝
A‑GCRT 将 OR‑Bench 过度拒绝从 25.7% 降至 17.4%，但未证明对自适应攻击的鲁棒性

deep_dive.overview: 本文提出 Wrapper‑Based Intent‑Form Augmentation (WIFA)，在共享包装族下自动生成有害与良性意图组，使包装形式成为噪声变量。基于该数据层，设计两条微调路径：WIFA‑Boost 采用两阶段 LoRA SFT，先让模型忽视包装，再在校准集强化有害拒绝；A‑GCRT 在训练时加入组内方差正则与有害/良性锚点，使同意图的不同包装得到一致且方向分离的决策分数。实验在 Qwen2.5‑7B 与 Llama‑3.1‑8B 上验证，显著提升有害拒绝并降低过度拒绝。

methodology.title: WIFA 数据构建
methodology.detail: 对每个有害意图 zh，生成 7 种包装 w(zh) 并加入 2 条直接拒绝锚点；对每个良性意图 zb，生成同样的 7 种包装 w(zb)。共计 2250 条有害示例、3500 条良性包装示例，形成 5750 条 WIFA‑SFT 数据。

methodology.title: WIFA‑Boost 两阶段训练
methodology.detail: Stage 1：在全部 5750 条 WIFA‑SFT 上进行 LoRA‑SFT，得到 θ1；Stage 2：在 2750 条校准集（含相同有害示例 + 500 条纯良性示例）上继续 LoRA‑SFT，得到最终参数 θ2。

methodology.title: A‑GCRT 组一致性与锚点正则
methodology.detail: 对每个意图组 G(z) 计算决策分数均值 s̄z，最小化组内方差 Lvar；同时对有害组施加正向锚点、对良性组施加负向锚点，使两组分数跨越设定 margin。

mechanism.title: 意图组监督
mechanism.detail: 将相同底层意图的不同包装视为同一监督单元，使模型学习意图而非包装特征，从而防止包装捷径。

mechanism.title: 组内方差正则
mechanism.detail: Lvar = Var_{x∈G(z)}(s(x)) 强制同意图的不同包装产生相近的决策分数，提升包装鲁棒性。

mechanism.title: 方向锚点
mechanism.detail: 在损失中加入 margin‑based 项，使有害组分数 ≥ +margin，良性组分数 ≤ –margin，确保决策在意图维度上分离。

experiments.title: 模型与基准
experiments.detail: 评估 Qwen2.5‑7B‑Instruct 与 Llama‑3.1‑8B‑Instruct；基准包括 HarmBench、SORRY‑Bench、OR‑Bench‑Hard、XSTest、MMLU、GSM8K，以及 15 种未见攻击族。

experiments.title: 对比方法
experiments.detail: 再现的提示时防御：Self‑Reminder、Intention Analysis、Goal Priority；训练时防御：Vanilla Refusal‑SFT、LookAhead Tuning、RATIONAL；以及外部参考 SIRL。

experiments.title: 指标
experiments.detail: HB、SB、OR、XS SafeRef/UnsafeRef、StrongREJECT、ASR、MMLU、GSM8K 等，以百分比或准确率呈现。

findings.title: 有害拒绝提升
findings.detail: WIFA‑Boost 在 Qwen 设置实现最高的 transformed‑harmful refusal（表 1 中最高 SB 分数）。

findings.title: 过度拒绝降低
findings.detail: A‑GCRT 将 OR‑Bench 过度拒绝率从基线 25.7% 降至 17.4%，优于所有再现防御。

findings.title: 跨模型一致性
findings.detail: 在 Llama 实验中同样观察到有害拒绝提升与过度拒绝下降，支持意图组解释的可迁移性。

findings.title: 消融验证
findings.detail: 去除匹配良性包装或改变两阶段顺序会削弱效果，证明数据结构与阶段顺序是关键因素。

contributions: 自动化意图组数据增强方法 WIFA，无需外部教师或手工标签
两种基于 WIFA 的安全微调路径：WIFA‑Boost 与 Anchored Group‑Consistent Refusal Training (A‑GCRT)
在主流模型上实现显著的有害拒绝提升与过度拒绝降低
limitations: 未声称在所有模型或数据分布上均能实现低于基线的过度拒绝
对自适应 jailbreak 攻击的鲁棒性缺乏实验验证
实验仅覆盖中文/英文两种模型，未评估多语言或更大规模模型
open_questions: 意图组监督在更大规模 LLM 或多语言环境下的可扩展性如何？
自适应攻击者是否能发现新的包装方式突破组一致性约束？
如何将意图组监督与推理时安全防御（如自我提醒）有效结合？

papers.title: From Safety Documentation to Safety Knowledge Support: An Evidence-Grounded LLM Framework for Medical Devices
papers.abstract: Medical devices are becoming more software-intensive, connected, and AI-enabled. Their development requires risk-management evidence aligned with ISO 14971 and, for software, IEC 62304. This evidence must be kept consistent across requirements, design decisions, software changes, verification results, complaints, and post-market data. These tasks are costly and depend on scarce safety and domain experts. Large language models (LLMs) may reduce parts of this effort because medical-device safety work is highly document-based. However, current LLM-based safety-engineering studies often address isolated methods, rely on generic prompting or public examples, and provide limited support for source links, traceability, uncertainty handling, lifecycle updates, and recorded expert review. This limits their use in regulated medical-device development. This paper argues that the central research problem is not safety-text generation, but source-linked safety-knowledge support. We propose an evidence-grounded framework that connects device artifacts, controlled knowledge storage and retrieval, method-specific generation of candidate safety items, critique and uncertainty checks, and recorded expert review. The framework prepares, links, checks, and updates candidate safety artifacts for expert decision-making. It does not decide whether a device is safe and does not provide regulatory approval. We also outline an evaluation strategy using non-public or newly built medical-device case studies and expert reference analyses to assess coverage, correctness, relevance, traceability, duplicate rate, unsupported claims, and review effort.

summary.takeaway: 该框架通过证据链接实现面向医疗器械的安全知识支持，帮助专家在整个生命周期中追踪和审查安全文档。
summary.problem: 医疗器械安全分析需在ISO 14971和IEC 62304框架下保持跨文档、跨阶段的可追溯证据，现有LLM方法缺乏源链接和不确定性处理。
summary.method: 提出一个证据‑grounded的框架，连接设备工件、受控知识库检索、方法特定生成、批评与不确定性检查以及记录的专家审查。
summary.evidence: 论文仅提供框架设计和基于非公开案例的评估方案，未呈现实际实验结果。
summary.limitations: 缺乏公开实验数据和量化评估，依赖于未公开的医疗器械案例。
summary.why_for_you: 若你关注可追溯、安全的LLM辅助医疗器械研发，此框架的证据链接思路与评估指标值得参考。

signals.text: 提出证据‑grounded安全知识支持框架，覆盖文档追溯与专家审查。
框架包括受控知识库检索、方法特定生成、批评与不确定性检查。

deep_dive.overview: 医疗器械安全分析在ISO 14971和IEC 62304要求下需保持跨需求、设计、验证等工件的可追溯证据，现有LLM辅助方法缺乏源链接和不确定性标记。作者提出一个证据‑grounded框架，将设备工件、受控知识库检索、方法特定生成、批评与不确定性检查以及记录的专家审查串联，实现安全文档的准备、链接、检查和更新。论文进一步规划了使用非公开或新建医疗器械案例的评估策略，以覆盖率、正确性、相关性、可追溯性、重复率、无依据主张和审查工作量等指标进行验证。

methodology.title: 受控知识库检索
methodology.detail: 构建并维护与医疗器械安全相关的结构化知识库，支持基于工件的检索以提供证据来源。

methodology.title: 方法特定生成与批评
methodology.detail: 针对不同安全分析任务（如危害识别、风险控制）使用专门的LLM提示生成候选项，并通过批评模块检查不确定性和潜在错误。

methodology.title: 记录的专家审查
methodology.detail: 将生成的候选安全项、证据链接和不确定性标记呈现给专家，记录审查决策以实现可追溯性。

mechanism.title: 证据‑grounded 链接
mechanism.detail: 每个LLM生成的安全条目必须关联到知识库中的具体文档或工件，实现来源可追溯。

mechanism.title: 不确定性指示
mechanism.detail: 系统在生成过程中标记置信度或潜在歧义，供专家在审查时重点关注。

experiments.title: 评估策略概述

papers.title: Asymptotic Risk Calibration for Selective Question Answering
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may generate fluent but incorrect answers, making uncertainty quantification important for reliable question answering. However, heuristic uncertainty scores cannot perfectly distinguish correct predictions from incorrect ones, and directly applying a fixed uncertainty threshold provides no statistical control over the error rate among accepted answers. To address this limitation, we propose A-CRC-QA, a post-hoc calibration framework for uncertainty-aware selective question answering. The proposed method reformulates selection-conditioned error control as a linear expectation constraint and applies a monotonized empirical-risk calibration procedure inspired by conformal risk control. Since the resulting instance-wise loss is generally non-monotone with respect to the acceptance threshold, our framework targets asymptotic rather than finite-sample risk control. A-CRC-QA is model-agnostic, requires no additional training, and can be combined with different uncertainty estimators. Experiments on CoQA and MedMCQA demonstrate its applicability to both open-ended and closed-ended question answering, achieving a favorable trade-off between accepted-answer reliability and answer retention compared with uncalibrated and confidence-bound-based baselines.

summary.takeaway: A-CRC-QA 在选择性问答中实现了渐近风险校准，提升接受率的同时保持错误率在用户设定阈值内。
summary.problem: 现有不确定性阈值无法提供对接受答案错误率的统计控制，导致在不同模型或数据上表现不稳。
summary.method: 提出将选择条件错误控制重新表述为线性期望约束，并使用单调化经验风险校准，加入渐近消失的有限样本校正。
summary.evidence: 在 CoQA 与 MedMCQA 上，A-CRC-QA 将违规率分别从 25.5% 降至 12.5% 与 19.0% 降至 8.0%，并提升接受率约 7%。
summary.limitations: 仅提供渐近风险控制，仍存在非零违规率，缺乏有限样本的高置信度保证。
summary.why_for_you: 若关注可信 LLM，A-CRC-QA 提供了基于统计校准的答案不确定性处理方案。

signals.text: A-CRC-QA 在目标风险 0.15 下提升约 7% 接受率并保持误差控制

deep_dive.overview: 本文针对 LLM 生成答案的可信度问题，提出 A-CRC-QA 框架，通过将选择性错误率约束转化为线性期望约束，并在经验风险上进行单调化处理，加入渐近消失的有限样本校正，实现对接受答案的渐近风险控制。实验在开放式 CoQA 与闭式 MedMCQA 两大基准上，使用 LLaMA‑3.1‑8B‑Instruct 与 Qwen2.5‑7B‑Instruct，比较多种基线，展示了在保持目标错误率的前提下显著提升接受率和功效。

methodology.title: 线性期望约束重构
methodology.detail: 将选择条件错误率表达为对接受阈值的线性期望约束，以便在校准阶段直接求解满足约束的阈值。

methodology.title: 单调化经验风险校准
methodology.detail: 对每个实例的非单调损失构造单调上包络，再在校准集上求平均，得到单调化的经验风险曲线。

methodology.title: 渐近消失的有限样本校正
methodology.detail: 在经验风险约束上加入随校准集规模 n→∞ 而消失的校正项，确保在大样本下风险趋近目标水平。

mechanism.title: 渐近风险控制原理
mechanism.detail: 通过 CRC 风格的校正，使得在校准集足够大时，选取的阈值使得测试集的选择性错误率在期望上不超过用户设定的 α。

mechanism.title: 单调化保证稳定性
mechanism.detail: 单调化处理消除经验风险曲线的局部波动，防止阈值因噪声产生过度保守或过度激进的选择。

experiments.title: 实验设置
experiments.detail: 数据集：CoQA（开放式）和 MedMCQA（多选）。模型：LLaMA‑3.1‑8B‑Instruct、Qwen2.5‑7B‑Instruct。基线：Fixed‑50、Empirical、UCB‑HFD、UCB‑CLP、LEC‑Direct。指标：SCER、AR、Power、VR、IF、AUROC。使用 100 次独立校准‑测试划分。

findings.title: 接受率提升
findings.detail: 在目标风险 α=0.15 下，A-CRC-QA 相比 UCB‑CLP 在 CoQA 上提升 7.2% 接受率，在 MedMCQA 上提升 7.4%。

findings.title: 违规率降低
findings.detail: CoQA 上违规率从 25.5% 降至 12.5%，MedMCQA 上从 19.0% 降至 8.0%。

findings.title: 功效提升
findings.detail: 接受的正确答案比例（Power）随接受率提升而同步增长，表明新增接受的答案主要为正确。

contributions: 提出 A-CRC-QA 渐近风险校准框架用于选择性问答
引入单调化经验风险与渐近校正的组合机制
在开放式与闭式 QA 基准上实现更优的风险‑接受率权衡
limitations: 仅提供渐近风险控制，未能保证有限样本的高置信度风险上界
违规率仍非零，说明在小校准集或极端分布下仍可能失控
方法依赖校准集大小，性能随 n 增大而改善

papers.title: NetlistBench: Evaluating LLM Reliability in SPICE Netlist Recognition and Manipulation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in circuit design workflows, yet their reliability on simulator-facing SPICE netlist recognition and manipulation remains poorly understood and is rarely separated from high-level design reasoning. Although netlists are textual, they encode structured circuit objects through topology and parameters. We present \textbf{NetlistBench}, a structure-verified benchmark for SPICE netlist recognition and manipulation. NetlistBench contains 2,342 cases across 24 task families, covering parameter and connectivity recognition and edits, hierarchical operations, equivalence judgment, and long-horizon compound editing. Model outputs are evaluated by a deterministic structure-aware oracle. Across six non-thinking LLMs, performance varies substantially with operation-level structural complexity. Simple local edits reach $96\%$--$100\%$ accuracy, while device addition drops to $41\%$--$83\%$ and equivalence judgment to $49\%$--$90\%$. Enabling reasoning substantially improves weaker models but does not eliminate structure-preservation failures, with performance still degrading sharply as the edit horizon increases. NetlistBench identifies netlist reliability as a distinct bottleneck for trustworthy LLM-based circuit design automation.

summary.evidence: Device addition accuracy drops to 41%–83%, and equivalence judgment to 49%–90% across six non-thinking LLMs.
summary.limitations: Focus on specific netlist tasks without broader circuit design integration.

summary.takeaway: NetlistBench identifies SPICE netlist reliability as a critical bottleneck for trustworthy LLM-based circuit design.

papers.title: Pragmatic Attack Surface: Vulnerabilities of Implicit Context in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: In the era of large language models (LLMs), attackers often manipulate natural language to elicit unsafe or harmful outputs, creating a new natural language attack surface unique to LLM-based systems, where attacks directly exploit explicit linguistic cues in user prompts to bypass the safety mechanism of LLMs. However, such attacks can often be mitigated by existing safety alignment algorithms. On the other hand, human language is inherently grounded in pragmatics, necessitating typical context to interpret language, e.g., world knowledge, social norms. However, such contexts are often implicit because they are not directly expressed in human language and are not sufficiently leveraged in safety alignment, creating a fundamental mismatch between human language interpretation and safety alignment approaches. In this paper, we demonstrate that this mismatch exposes vulnerabilities in LLMs. We refer to this vulnerability as the pragmatic attack surface, which can be exploited to achieve high attack success rates. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms baseline attack methods across various open-source and closed-source models by a substantial margin.

summary.takeaway: 利用隐含前提的pragmatic attack能够在安全对齐模型上实现几乎完美的攻击成功率。
summary.problem: 现有安全对齐仅检测显式有害语言，忽视了人类语言中的隐式语用上下文。
summary.method: 通过两轮提示先让模型推断情境的presupposition，再生成语义不同但语用等价的有害输出。
summary.evidence: 在BBQ、Hate、PolyGuard等基准上，对Claude Opus等模型的非拒绝率和攻击成功率均显著高于Direct Prompt、ActorAttack和Crescendo。
summary.limitations: 仅在涉及隐式歧视、刻板印象和隐性仇恨的任务上评估，未探索其他语用现象或更广泛的任务。
summary.why_for_you: 对可信LLM研究者而言，该工作揭示了新的攻击面并提供了蓝队强化语用推理的研究方向。

signals.text: 提出‘pragmatic attack surface’概念并展示利用暗示推理的高效攻击
两轮提示先抽取隐含前提，再生成语义不同但语用等价的有害输出
在BBQ等基准上攻击成功率接近100%，但仅限于隐式歧视等任务

deep_dive.overview: 本文指出安全对齐模型忽视了语言的隐式语用上下文，定义了pragmatic attack surface，并提出一种两步提示方法：先让模型识别情境的presupposition，随后在该隐式上下文下生成语义多样但语用等价的有害内容。实验在多个公开基准和闭源模型上验证了该攻击的高成功率，同时通过消融实验确认presupposition步骤是关键因素。

methodology.detail: 向目标模型询问给定情境背后的隐含前提，以显式化未表达的社会规范或世界知识。

methodology.title: Scenario Generation Turn
methodology.detail: 基于推断出的前提生成满足该前提的具体情境描述，保持语义与原始请求等价。

methodology.title: Harmful Output Turn
methodology.detail: 在构造的情境中请求模型产生有害内容，利用安全机制对显式线索的盲点。

mechanism.title: Pragmatic Inference Exploitation
mechanism.detail: 通过让模型自行构建隐式上下文，使安全过滤器难以捕捉因缺少显式危害词而产生的有害输出。

experiments.title: Benchmark & Model Setup
experiments.detail: 使用BBQ（500例）、Hate、PolyGuard三套社会危害基准；评估模型包括Claude Opus、其他开源与闭源LLM。基线包括Direct Prompt、ActorAttack、Crescendo，攻击查询由DeepSeek‑v4‑Flash生成。

experiments.title: Metrics
experiments.detail: 报告Non‑Refusal Rate（是否拒绝生成）和AttackSuccess Rate（DeepSeek分类器判断输出是否有害）。

experiments.title: Results
experiments.detail: 在所有模型上，本文方法的Non‑Refusal Rate和AttackSuccess Rate均显著高于基线，尤其在Claude Opus上接近100%成功率。

experiments.title: Ablation
experiments.detail: 去除presupposition回合后，攻击成功率下降，验证该步骤对提升攻击效果至关重要。

findings.title: High Success Across Models
findings.detail: 利用隐式前提的攻击在开源和闭源模型上均实现近乎完美的成功率，表明安全对齐对语用线索的盲点普遍存在。

findings.title: Presupposition Critical
findings.detail: 消融实验显示，缺失presupposition回合会显著降低攻击成功率，证明语用推理是核心机制。

papers.title: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: The safety of large language model (LLM) agents depends not only on model weights but also on the agent harness that manages context, memory, tools, permissions, and runtime control. Existing safety mechanisms often treat the harness as a fixed deployment artifact, limiting their ability to evolve with emerging risks. Moreover, coupled functions across harness components obscure safety responsibility attribution, making localized evolution difficult. We propose Safety Harness Evolution (SHE), a framework that learns evolving safe boundaries from rollout trajectories. SHE decomposes the harness into four artifacts with explicit safety responsibilities, including the System Prompt, Rule Bank, Safety Memory, and Tool Policy, defining clear functional boundaries for localized evolution. Based on this decomposition, SHE introduces an attribution-guided evolution loop that converts trajectory failures into structured diagnoses, learns artifact-specific boundary refinements, and selects evolved harnesses through safety-utility validation. Experiments on Agent-SafetyBench demonstrate that SHE effectively enhances safety through harness evolution, achieving a 3.1x ASR reduction compared with static SafeHarness, while also improving benign utility. The evolved harness further generalizes to unseen risks on the held-out AgentHarm benchmark and transfers across agent models without additional evolution.

summary.takeaway: SHE通过从执行轨迹学习并局部演化安全套件，实现显著的安全性提升。
summary.problem: 静态安全套件无法随新风险演化，且组件耦合导致难以定位改进。
summary.method: 将安全套件拆分为系统提示、规则库、安全记忆、工具策略四个可编辑部件，并通过归因驱动的演化循环从轨迹诊断到局部编辑。
summary.evidence: 在Agent‑SafetyBench上ASR降低3.1倍，且在AgentHarm上危害分数从19.8%降至9.8%。
summary.limitations: 仅在离线基准上评估，缺乏真实部署验证。
summary.why_for_you: 关注LLM安全的你可借鉴其可演化套件设计与归因机制。

signals.text: 提出SHE框架，将安全套件拆解为四个可编辑部件并实现轨迹驱动演化

deep_dive.overview: SHE将LLM代理的安全套件功能解耦为系统提示、规则库、安全记忆和工具策略四个明确责任的可编辑部件。基于归因驱动的演化循环，系统从执行轨迹中诊断风险、路由至对应部件、进行有界编辑，并通过安全‑效用验证挑选最佳套件。实验在Agent‑SafetyBench和AgentHarm两大基准上展示了显著的安全提升与效用保持，且可跨模型迁移。

methodology.title: 归因驱动的演化循环（Algorithm 1）
methodology.detail: 在每轮演化中收集轨迹τ与安全‑效用记录oi，使用RiskRelevant筛选风险案例，生成结构化风险诊断zi并路由至artifact ri，随后执行Edit生成候选Δ，经过ValidEdit和安全‑效用选择后更新Hbest。

mechanism.title: 结构化风险诊断与部件路由
mechanism.detail: 将每个失败轨迹映射为包含危害域、攻击面、失败模式的风险记录zi，并依据这些维度将诊断路由至最相关的artifact ri，实现定位式改进。

mechanism.title: 有界编辑与安全‑效用选择
mechanism.detail: 编辑仅在指定artifact范围内进行有界修改，随后通过ValidEdit检查合法性，并在安全分数SΩ和效用分数UΩ的约束下挑选接受的候选套件。

experiments.title: 实验设置
experiments.detail: 使用Agent‑SafetyBench（200任务，5种攻击）和AgentHarm（440条有害行为）两套基准；对比无防御、System Prompt、LlamaFirewall、SafeHarness、PROGENT、MemskillSafeHarness等静态与自适应基线；指标包括Clean UBR、ASR、UA、Harm Score、Harm Refusal、Benign NR。

findings.title: 安全性提升
findings.detail: SHE将Agent‑SafetyBench的平均ASR从17.1%降至5.5%（3.1×降低），Clean UBR从25.7%降至19.8%。

findings.title: 效用保持与提升
findings.detail: 在相同基准上，SHE的平均UA从31.6提升至47.6%。

findings.title: 跨模型与未见风险的泛化
findings.detail: 在AgentHarm上，演化后套件将Harm Score从19.8%降至9.8%，Harm Refusal提升至86.4%，且无需额外演化即可迁移至其他代理模型。

将套件功能解耦为四个可编辑artifact
设计归因驱动的演化循环实现局部、可验证的改进
在两个大规模代理安全基准上实现显著的安全与效用提升

演化过程依赖大量标注轨迹，未量化数据收集成本
